name: request_cancel

completed or already cancelled.

signature: int32_t basalt_entity_of_player(int32_t player)

entity_of_player: the entity handle of an online player (the same player always gives the same handle). Arguments:
a player handle. Result: the entity handle, STALE for a player that left, INVALID for a malformed handle.

name: entity_player
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_player(int32_t entity)
doc:
entity_player: the player handle of an entity that is a player. Result: the player handle, ABSENT when the entity
is not a player, STALE for a gone entity.

name: entity_release
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_release(int32_t entity)
doc:
entity_release: forgets a handle so its slot can be reused. OK, or STALE when it was not live. The entity itself is
untouched.

name: entity_alive
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_alive(int32_t entity)
doc:
entity_alive: 1 while the entity is in the world, 0 once it left (also for a handle kept past its death); INVALID
for a malformed handle. Never answers STALE.

name: entity_id
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_id(int32_t entity)
doc:
entity_id: the numeric id the world and the events use for this entity. Result: the id (a positive i32), STALE or
INVALID.

name: entity_by_id
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_by_id(const char *world, int32_t wlen, int32_t id)
doc:
entity_by_id: the entity with that numeric id in a world. Arguments: world name, id. Result: the handle, ABSENT when
no live entity of that world has the id, ABSENT for an unknown world.

name: entity_by_uuid
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_by_uuid(const char *uuid, int32_t ulen)
doc:
entity_by_uuid: the live entity with that UUID text in any world. Result: the handle, ABSENT, INVALID for a text
that is not a UUID.

name: entity_query
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_query(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *query, int32_t qlen, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_query: the entities of a world that match a query, as an array of i32 handles written to `out` (count
entries fit in `cap` entries; the result is the number of handles, written only when they fit). Query value, all
keys optional (an empty query, len 0, matches every entity of the world): "type" (an entity type id, or a list of
them; "minecraft:" may be left out), "x" "y" "z" with "radius" (a sphere; all four needed), "min_x" "min_y" "min_z"
"max_x" "max_y" "max_z" (a box; all six needed), "chunk_x" "chunk_z" (the entities of that chunk, both needed),
"limit" (at most that many). Result: the count, ABSENT for an unknown world, INVALID for a bad query.

name: entity_types
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_types(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: entity_types: every entity type id the server knows, as a value list of strings. Needed-length result.

name: entity_type_attributes
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_type_attributes(const char *type, int32_t tlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_type_attributes: the attributes a new living entity of the type starts with, as a value map from attribute id
to its base value (an empty map for a type that is not living). Result: the needed length, INVALID for an unknown
type.

name: entity_spawn
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_spawn(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *type, int32_t tlen, double x, double y, double z, const char *opts, int32_t olen)
doc:
entity_spawn: puts a new entity of `type` in the world at x, y, z. Options value (len 0 for none): "yaw" (f64,
default 0), "reason" (string for the entity.spawn event, default "plugin"). Result: the handle; ABSENT when the
entity.spawn event was cancelled or the server refused the spawn; INVALID for an unknown world or type.

name: entity_spawn_nbt
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_spawn_nbt(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen, const char *cause, int32_t clen)
doc:
entity_spawn_nbt: brings back an entity from named NBT bytes (what entity_snapshot gave). `cause` is the reason the
entity.spawn event reports (empty means "plugin"). Result: the handle, ABSENT when a listener cancelled it, INVALID
for bad NBT or an unknown world.

name: entity_drop_item
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_drop_item(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *item, int32_t ilen, double x, double y, double z, double vx, double vy, double vz)
doc:
entity_drop_item: puts an item on the ground with a velocity. The item is a value map: "id" (string, required) and
"count" (default 1), or "nbt" (the bytes of a whole saved stack, which replaces the other keys). Result: the handle of
the item entity, ABSENT when nothing was dropped, INVALID for a bad item or world.

name: entity_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_remove(int32_t entity)
doc: entity_remove: takes the entity out of the world (a player is not removed: INVALID). OK, STALE.

name: entity_remove_uuid
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_remove_uuid(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *uuid, int32_t ulen)
doc:
entity_remove_uuid: takes the entity with that UUID out of the world. OK, ABSENT when no live entity has it,
INVALID for a text that is not a UUID or an unknown world.

name: entity_position
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_position(int32_t entity, double *out)
doc: entity_position: writes x, y, z as three f64 to `out` (24 bytes). OK, STALE, INVALID for a bad pointer.

name: entity_teleport
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_teleport(int32_t entity, double x, double y, double z, const char *opts, int32_t olen)
doc:
entity_teleport: moves the entity to x, y, z. Options value (len 0 for none): "yaw" and "pitch" (f64, kept when
absent), "world" (a world name; a different world is moved to only for players, any other entity answers INVALID).
OK, STALE, INVALID, ABSENT for an unknown world, DENIED when a plugin event handler refused the teleport.

name: entity_velocity
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_velocity(int32_t entity, double *out)
doc:
entity_velocity: writes the velocity (blocks per tick) as three f64 to `out` (24 bytes). OK, STALE, INVALID for a
player (a player's motion belongs to its client).

name: entity_set_velocity
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_set_velocity(int32_t entity, double x, double y, double z)
doc: entity_set_velocity: replaces the velocity. OK, STALE, INVALID when the entity cannot be pushed.

name: entity_rotation
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_rotation(int32_t entity, double *out)
doc: entity_rotation: writes yaw and pitch in degrees as two f64 to `out` (16 bytes). OK, STALE, INVALID.

name: entity_set_rotation
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_set_rotation(int32_t entity, double yaw, double pitch)
doc: entity_set_rotation: turns the entity. OK, STALE, INVALID when it cannot be turned.

name: entity_get
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_get(int32_t entity, const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_get: one property by name, written as a value. Besides the table of entity_properties these base names
always exist: "id" "type" "world" "uuid" "alive" "x" "y" "z" "yaw" "pitch" "on_ground" "age" "width" "height"
"custom_name", "pos" and "velocity" (maps with keys x, y, z). A property that does not apply to this kind of entity
reads as null. Result: the needed length, ABSENT for an unknown name, STALE, INVALID.

name: entity_set
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_set(int32_t entity, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
entity_set: writes one property by name from a value (a number, bool, string or list of strings as the property
wants; "velocity" takes a map with x, y, z; "yaw", "pitch" and "custom_name" are writable base names). OK, ABSENT
for an unknown name, INVALID for a read-only property or a value the entity refuses, STALE.

name: entity_call
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_call(int32_t entity, const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_call: runs one named operation (damage, kill, add_effect, attribute, equipment, mount, move_to, find_path,
add_goal, brain_set_memory, merge_nbt, ...; see entity_operations). `args` is a value list of the operation's
arguments in order (len 0 for none); the result is the operation's value written to `out`: a bool, number, string,
bytes (NBT), a list, or for operations that return rows a list of maps keyed by the columns of entity_operations.
Results that are ids (passengers, path nodes) are integers. Result: the needed length, ABSENT for an unknown
operation or one the entity cannot do, STALE, INVALID for a bad argument list.

name: entity_properties
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_properties(int32_t entity, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_properties: the property names an entity answers, as a value list of maps with "name" (string) and
"writable" (bool), built from the server's real tables for this kind of entity (a player or any other entity).
Needed-length result, STALE, INVALID.

name: entity_operations
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_operations(int32_t entity, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_operations: the operation names entity_call accepts for this entity, as a value list of maps with "name"
(string) and "columns" (a list of strings, empty unless the operation returns rows). Needed-length result, STALE,
INVALID.

name: entity_snapshot
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_snapshot(int32_t entity, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_snapshot: the entity as the named NBT compound the world would save (id, Pos, Rotation, Motion, UUID, ...),
written as raw bytes (not a value). Needed-length result, STALE, INVALID for a player.

name: entity_restore
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_restore(int32_t entity, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen)
doc:
entity_restore: applies saved NBT bytes to the live entity in place, as /data merge entity does. OK, STALE,
INVALID for a player or malformed NBT.

name: entity_spawn_rules
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_spawn_rules(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *rules, int32_t rlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_spawn_rules: reads and optionally changes the natural spawning rules of a world. `rules` is a value (len 0 to
only read) with optional keys "limits" and "ticks_per" (maps from a mob category to an integer; a negative value
restores vanilla; categories monster, creature, ambient, axolotls, underground_water_creature, water_creature,
water_ambient, misc), "allow_monsters" and "allow_animals" (bool). The result map written to `out` holds the same
keys with what a plugin changed (categories left at vanilla are left out). Needed-length result, ABSENT for an
unknown world, INVALID for a bad value.

name: entity_mechanic
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_mechanic(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
entity_mechanic: one of the server's stateless entity formulas by name, so plugins get vanilla's exact numbers. The
arguments are a value map and the answer a value, both per name:
  combat.after_armor {damage, armor, toughness, fraction_add?} -> f64
  combat.after_protection {damage, protection} -> f64
  combat.after_resistance {damage, amplifier} -> f64
  combat.after_difficulty {damage, difficulty} -> f64 ("peaceful", "easy", "normal", "hard")
  combat.scales_with_difficulty {scaling, caused_by_living_non_player?} -> bool
  combat.absorb {damage, absorption} -> {health, absorption}
  combat.fall_damage {distance, safe?} -> i64
  breeding.offspring_attribute {a, b, min, max, first, second, third} -> f64
  physics.clip {box, from, to} -> point or null; physics.collide {colliders, box, movement} -> point
  physics.step_up {colliders, grounded, grounded_offset_y, movement, max_up_step, reach_squared} -> point or null
  physics.rotate_towards_movement {motion, x_rot_o, y_rot_o, x_rot, y_rot, speed} -> map or null
  physics.closest_hit {candidates, from, to, margin} -> {index, point} or null
  physics.picked_hit {candidates, root, from, to, max} -> {index, point} or null
  physics.projectile_margin {tick_count} -> f64; physics.leash_angular_friction {on_ground, block_friction?, in_liquid?}
  physics.shulker_box {size, direction, progress_from, progress_to, position} -> box
  physics.leash_pull {self, holder, quad?, slack?, self_motion, holder_motion, known_motion} -> {torque, push} or null
A point is a list of three f64, a box a map with min_x min_y min_z max_x max_y max_z, a collider a box map plus
"shape" (i64), a candidate a box map plus "pick_radius", "pick_from_inside" and "root", a leash body a map with
position, width, height and yaw. Index results are 1-based. Needed-length result, ABSENT for an unknown name,
INVALID for a bad argument. Callable on any thread.

name: entity_event_entity
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_event_entity(int32_t ctx)
doc:
entity_event_entity: the handle of the entity an entity.* event is about (its "entity_id" field). Result: the
handle, INVALID for a ctx that is not an event with an entity, ABSENT when that entity is gone, STALE once the
callback returned.

name: entity_ai_answer
signature: int32_t basalt_entity_ai_answer(int32_t ctx, int32_t result)
doc:
entity_ai_answer: answers the goal or behaviour question of this ctx (can_use, can_continue; the other phases
ignore it). OK, INVALID for any other ctx, STALE once the callback returned.

name: event_on_ex
signature: int32_t basalt_event_on_ex(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t priority, int32_t flags, const char *filters, int32_t flen, int32_t token)
doc:
event_on_ex: listens to `name` ("player.chat", "block.break", or a plugin event "plugin:topic" which has a colon)
and calls basalt_callback(token, ctx). `priority` is BASALT_PRIORITY_*, `flags` the BASALT_EVENT_* bits.
`filters` is one value, a map from field name to the value the field must equal (same kind, an i64 never equals an
f64) for the listener to run; ptr 0 and len 0 mean no filter. A post listener (BASALT_EVENT_POST) runs after the
decision, on a copy: event_set answers INVALID and event_cancel changes nothing. BASALT_EVENT_CANCELLED on an event
that cannot be cancelled is INVALID. Plugin events accept no filters and no flags but priority.
OK; INVALID for an unknown event, a bad priority, flags, a filter on a field the event lacks or a malformed map.

name: event_name
signature: int32_t basalt_event_name(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
event_name: the event's name into `out`; the length it needs. STALE outside the callback, INVALID for a ctx that is
not an event.

name: event_get
signature: int32_t basalt_event_get(int32_t ctx, const char *field, int32_t flen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
event_get: one field as a value (the encoding of basalt_values.h) into `out`; the length it needs. An unset field
is the null value. The names "name" and "uuid" stand for player_name and player_uuid, and "online" on a player event
is the number of players online. ABSENT when the event has no such field; STALE, INVALID as event_name.

name: event_set
signature: int32_t basalt_event_set(int32_t ctx, const char *field, int32_t flen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
event_set: replaces one field with the value at (value, vlen). Only fields the event lists as mutable can be set.
A number keeps the kind the field has (an i64 sent to an f64 field is converted, an f64 sent to an i64 field must be
whole); a field the server left unset takes any scalar kind; null unsets. OK; INVALID for a field that is not
mutable or does not exist, a value that does not fit the field, a post listener or a plugin event; STALE.

name: event_fields
signature: int32_t basalt_event_fields(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: event_fields: every field of the event with its current value, as one map, into `out`. The needed length.

name: event_describe
signature: int32_t basalt_event_describe(const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
event_describe: what the server declares for event `name`, as the map {name: string, cancellable: bool,
custom: bool, fields: list of {name: string, mutable: bool}}, into `out`. The tables come from the server's own event
definitions. ABSENT for an unknown name.

name: event_names
signature: int32_t basalt_event_names(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: event_names: the list of every event name the server declares, as a value, sorted. The needed length.

name: event_cancelled
signature: int32_t basalt_event_cancelled(int32_t ctx)
doc: event_cancelled: 1 when the event is cancelled so far, 0 when not. STALE, INVALID as event_name.

name: event_cancel_with
signature: int32_t basalt_event_cancel_with(int32_t ctx, const char *text, int32_t tlen, const char *args, int32_t alen)
doc:
event_cancel_with: cancels the event and keeps a message for whoever caused it: `text` is a lang key when it starts
with '@', else MiniMessage, with arguments as in basalt_player_send. OK; INVALID when the event cannot be cancelled
or this is a post listener; ABSENT when the lang key does not exist.

name: event_cancel_message
signature: int32_t basalt_event_cancel_message(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: event_cancel_message: the message given to event_cancel_with, into `out`; the needed length, ABSENT when none.

name: event_is_post
signature: int32_t basalt_event_is_post(int32_t ctx)
doc: event_is_post: 1 for a post listener, 0 for a decision listener. STALE, INVALID as event_name.

name: event_emit
signature: int32_t basalt_event_emit(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
event_emit: fires the plugin event `name` (it must contain a colon, "myplugin:level_up") with `value` as its
payload, one value of any shape. Every plugin that listens with event_on_ex runs, in priority order, on its own
thread turn; a listener of the emitting plugin does not run while the emitter is inside a callback (callbacks never
nest in one plugin). Returns how many listeners ran, 0 when nobody listens. INVALID for a name without a colon, a
malformed value or a chain of emits nested more than 8 deep.

name: event_payload
signature: int32_t basalt_event_payload(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: event_payload: the payload of a plugin event, into `out`; the needed length. INVALID for a server event.

name: player_by_uuid
signature: int32_t basalt_player_by_uuid(const char *uuid, int32_t len)
doc: player_by_uuid: the handle of the online player with that uuid text, 0 when none.

name: player_uuid
signature: int32_t basalt_player_uuid(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: player_uuid: the uuid text into `out`; the needed length. STALE for a player who left.

name: player_get
signature: int32_t basalt_player_get(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_get: one property by name as a value into `out`; the needed length. The names are the ones
basalt_player_describe lists plus health, food, gamemode, level, world, x, y, z, yaw, pitch, ping, sneaking,
flying, on_ground, held_item, address, permission_level and online. ABSENT when there is no such property;
STALE.

name: player_set
signature: int32_t basalt_player_set(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
player_set: writes one property by name from the value at (value, vlen). Writable names are health, food, gamemode,
level and every property basalt_player_describe marks writable. OK; INVALID for a read only or unknown name or a
value of the wrong kind; STALE.

name: player_call
signature: int32_t basalt_player_call(int32_t player, const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_call: runs the named operation (basalt_player_describe lists them) with `args`, a list value (ptr 0 and len 0
are an empty list), and writes its result as a value into `out`; the needed length. The result is null for an
operation with nothing to answer. Operations that report success answer a bool. ABSENT for an unknown operation;
INVALID for a malformed argument list; STALE.

name: player_describe
signature: int32_t basalt_player_describe(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_describe: the player property and operation tables the server defines, as {properties: list of
{name: string, kind: "bool"|"int"|"real"|"text"|"list", writable: bool}, operations: list of string}, into `out`.
The needed length.

name: player_health
signature: int32_t basalt_player_health(int32_t player, double *out)
doc: player_health: writes the health in half hearts to *out (an f64). OK; STALE.

name: player_set_health
signature: int32_t basalt_player_set_health(int32_t player, double health)
doc: player_set_health: sets the health. OK; INVALID for a negative or NaN value; STALE.

name: player_gamemode
signature: int32_t basalt_player_gamemode(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: player_gamemode: "survival", "creative", "adventure" or "spectator" into `out`; the needed length. STALE.

name: player_set_gamemode
signature: int32_t basalt_player_set_gamemode(int32_t player, const char *mode, int32_t mlen)
doc: player_set_gamemode: changes the game mode by name. OK; INVALID for an unknown name; STALE.

name: player_teleport
signature: int32_t basalt_player_teleport(int32_t player, const char *world, int32_t wlen, double x, double y, double z, float yaw, float pitch)
doc:
player_teleport: moves the player to (x, y, z) facing yaw and pitch in degrees, in `world` (an empty name is the
world the player is in). OK; ABSENT when the move could not be done (unknown world, nothing to teleport); INVALID for
NaN or an infinite coordinate; STALE.

name: player_title
signature: int32_t basalt_player_title(int32_t player, const char *title, int32_t tlen, const char *subtitle, int32_t slen, int32_t fade_in, int32_t stay, int32_t fade_out, const char *args, int32_t alen)

name: player_kick
signature: int32_t basalt_player_kick(int32_t player, const char *text, int32_t tlen, const char *args, int32_t alen)
doc:
player_kick: disconnects the player with the message (text rules of basalt_player_send). OK; ABSENT for a missing
lang key; STALE. The handle is STALE afterwards.

name: player_effect
signature: int32_t basalt_player_effect(int32_t player, const char *effect, int32_t elen, int32_t ticks, int32_t amplifier)
doc:
player_effect: gives a potion effect by id ("minecraft:speed") for `ticks` (-1 is endless) at `amplifier` (0 is
level one); 0 ticks removes it. OK; ABSENT for an unknown effect; INVALID for ticks below -1 or a negative
amplifier; STALE.

name: player_open_inventory
signature: int32_t basalt_player_open_inventory(int32_t player, const char *kind, int32_t klen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
player_open_inventory: opens a window of `kind` for the player. `spec` is one value (ptr 0 and len 0 for none).
Kinds: "merchant" ({title: string JSON text component, offers: string SNBT}), "trades" ({entity: i64 entity id of a
villager}), "sign" ({x, y, z: i64, front: bool}), "book" ({item: string SNBT of the written book}). The player's own
chest windows are menus (basalt_menu_open). OK; ABSENT when the server could not open it; INVALID for an unknown
kind or spec; STALE.

name: player_close_window
signature: int32_t basalt_player_close_window(int32_t player)
doc: player_close_window: closes the window the player has open. OK; STALE.

name: form_open
signature: int32_t basalt_form_open(int32_t player, const char *form, int32_t flen, int32_t token)
doc:
form_open: shows a form to the player. The form is one map {title: string, body: string or list of string,
buttons: list of string (default ["OK"]), fields: list of maps {key, type: "text"|"toggle"|"slider"|"choice",
label, initial, min, max, step, options}}; every text is a lang key with '@' or MiniMessage. Returns a request
handle and later calls basalt_callback(token, ctx) once, where basalt_value_result answers the map {player: i64
handle, button: i64 index from 0, values: map from field key to string, bool (toggle) or f64 (slider)}; the callback
does not run when the player closes the form or leaves, or after basalt_request_cancel. INVALID for a malformed
form; STALE.

name: form_close
signature: int32_t basalt_form_close(int32_t player)
doc: form_close: closes the form the player has open from this plugin and drops its completion. OK, ABSENT when none.

name: dialog_show
signature: int32_t basalt_dialog_show(int32_t player, const char *dialog, int32_t dlen, int32_t token)
doc:
dialog_show: shows a dialog to the player: `dialog` is a full dialog as SNBT (starts with '{') or the id of a
registry dialog. Returns a request handle and calls basalt_callback(token, ctx) once, on the first custom click
the player answers, where basalt_value_result answers {player: i64 handle, id: string, payload: string SNBT or
empty}; no answer means no callback (basalt_request_cancel drops it). ABSENT when the server could not show the
dialog; INVALID for malformed text; STALE.

name: dialog_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_dialog_clear(int32_t player)
doc: dialog_clear: closes the dialog the player has open. OK; STALE.

name: hud_scoreboard_main
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_main(void)
doc:
scoreboard_main: the handle of the main board. The same handle on every call, never STALE, and it cannot be
released (INVALID).

name: hud_scoreboard_create
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_create(void)
doc:
scoreboard_create: a new empty board of the plugin's own; its handle, or INVALID when scoreboards are not
available.

name: hud_scoreboard_release
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_release(int32_t board)
doc:
scoreboard_release: forgets a board made by scoreboard_create once nothing shows it. OK; STALE; INVALID for the main
board.

name: hud_scoreboard_list
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_list(int32_t board, const char *what, int32_t wlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
scoreboard_list: the names a board holds as a list of strings. `what` is "objectives", "entries" or "teams"
(anything else is INVALID). Result: the length of the encoded list; STALE for a bad board.

name: hud_objective_add
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_objective_add(int32_t board, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
objective_add: spec keys criterion (string, default "dummy"), title (text, default the name), hearts (bool, shows
the score as hearts). OK; INVALID when the name is taken or the criterion is unknown.

name: hud_objective_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_objective_remove(int32_t board, const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: objective_remove: OK; ABSENT when there is no such objective.

name: hud_display_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_display_set(int32_t board, const char *slot, int32_t slotlen, const char *objective, int32_t olen)
doc:
display_set: shows the objective in the slot; an empty objective name clears the slot. OK; INVALID for a bad slot;
ABSENT when the objective does not exist.

name: hud_display_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_display_get(int32_t board, const char *slot, int32_t slotlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
display_get: the name of the objective shown in the slot, written to `out`; its length. ABSENT when the slot is
empty; INVALID for a bad slot.

name: hud_score_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_score_get(int32_t board, const char *entry, int32_t elen, const char *objective, int32_t olen, int32_t *out)
doc: score_get: the entry's score in the objective, stored in `*out`. OK; ABSENT when the entry has none.

name: hud_score_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_score_set(int32_t board, const char *entry, int32_t elen, const char *objective, int32_t olen, int32_t value)
doc: score_set: OK; INVALID when the objective does not exist or is read only.

name: hud_score_reset
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_score_reset(int32_t board, const char *entry, int32_t elen, const char *objective, int32_t olen)
doc: score_reset: forgets the entry's score in the objective, or in every objective when `objective` is empty. OK.

name: hud_team_add
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_add(int32_t board, const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: team_add: OK; INVALID when the name is taken.

name: hud_team_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_set(int32_t board, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
team_set: spec keys display_name, prefix, suffix (text), color (a color name or "none"), friendly_fire and
see_invisible (bool), name_tags, death_messages (always, never, hideForOtherTeams, hideForOwnTeam) and collision
(always, never, pushOtherTeams, pushOwnTeam). OK; ABSENT when the team does not exist.

name: hud_team_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_remove(int32_t board, const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: team_remove: OK; ABSENT when there is no such team.

name: hud_team_join
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_join(int32_t board, const char *team, int32_t tlen, const char *entry, int32_t elen)
doc:
team_join: an entry (a player name or an entity uuid) joins the team and leaves the one it was on. OK; ABSENT when
the team does not exist.

name: hud_team_leave
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_leave(int32_t board, const char *team, int32_t tlen, const char *entry, int32_t elen)
doc: team_leave: OK; ABSENT when the entry is not on that team.

name: hud_team_of
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_team_of(int32_t board, const char *entry, int32_t elen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: team_of: the name of the team the entry is on, written to `out`; its length. ABSENT when on none.

name: hud_scoreboard_show
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_show(int32_t player, int32_t board)
doc:
scoreboard_show: draws the board for the player instead of the one they had. OK; STALE for a gone player or board.
Showing the main board puts the player back on the default.

name: hud_scoreboard_shown
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_scoreboard_shown(int32_t player)
doc:
scoreboard_shown: the handle of the board the player sees, when it is the main board or one the plugin holds.
ABSENT when it is a board of another plugin; STALE for a gone player.

name: hud_bossbar_create
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_create(const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc: bossbar_create: the new bar's handle. INVALID for a bad spec or when a kept bar of that key exists.

name: hud_bossbar_attach
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_attach(const char *id, int32_t ilen)
doc:
bossbar_attach: a handle for an existing bar by its id or key (from bossbar_kept or bossbar_get), so a plugin can
keep driving a kept bar after a restart. ABSENT when there is none. The handle is the plugin's to drop with
bossbar_remove only when it wants the bar deleted.

name: hud_bossbar_update
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_update(int32_t bar, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc: bossbar_update: applies the spec keys present. OK; STALE when the bar is gone; INVALID for a bad spec.

name: hud_bossbar_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_remove(int32_t bar)
doc: bossbar_remove: deletes the bar for everyone. OK; STALE.

name: hud_bossbar_player_add
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_player_add(int32_t bar, int32_t player)
doc:
bossbar_player_add and bossbar_player_remove: OK, also when the player was already in or out; STALE for a gone bar
or player.

name: hud_bossbar_player_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_player_remove(int32_t bar, int32_t player)

name: hud_bossbar_players
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_players(int32_t bar, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: bossbar_players: the uuids of the players shown the bar, as a list of strings. STALE for a gone bar.

name: hud_bossbar_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_get(int32_t bar, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
bossbar_get: a map with id, key (string or null), title, color, style, progress, darken_sky, boss_music, fog and
visible. The title is the server's text form. STALE for a gone bar.

name: hud_bossbar_kept
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_bossbar_kept(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: bossbar_kept: the ids of the kept bars as a list of strings.

name: hud_hologram_create
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_hologram_create(const char *world, int32_t wlen, const char *text, int32_t tlen, double x, double y, double z)
doc:
hologram_create: the new hologram's handle. ABSENT when the world does not exist or the lang key is missing;
INVALID when the server could not make it.

name: hud_hologram_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_hologram_set(int32_t hologram, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
hologram_set: spec keys text, x, y and z (a move, the three together), audience (a list of player names or uuids,
or null for everyone). OK; STALE; INVALID for a partial position or a key of the wrong type.

name: hud_hologram_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_hologram_get(int32_t hologram, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
hologram_get: a map with id (the entity id), world, x, y, z, alive, text and audience (a list of uuids or null).
STALE for a gone hologram.

name: hud_hologram_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_hologram_remove(int32_t hologram)
doc: hologram_remove: OK; STALE.

name: hud_npc_create
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_create(const char *spec, int32_t slen, int32_t token)
doc:
npc_create: spec keys world (default the default world), name (text), x, y, z, uuid (a fixed uuid), skin (a map
with texture and signature, or with name of an online player). `token` is the click callback, 0 for none. The new
NPC's handle (it has the attributes max_health and movement_speed); ABSENT for an unknown world; INVALID for a bad spec or when the server could not make it.

name: hud_npc_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_set(int32_t npc, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
npc_set: spec keys name, x, y, z (a move), yaw and pitch (a look), looks_at_players (bool), skin (as in create),
audience (a list of names or uuids, or null), health, held_slot (0 to 8), flags (the shared flags byte), pose (the
Pose ordinal), attributes (a map from attribute name to base value) and equipment (a map from a Bukkit slot number
as a string, 0 to 8 hotbar, 36 to 39 feet to head, 40 off hand, to a map with item and count, or null to clear).
Keys are applied in that order and OK is returned when all applied. INVALID for the first one that fails (an
attribute the NPC lacks, an unknown item); STALE when the NPC is gone.

name: hud_npc_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_get(int32_t npc, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
npc_get: a map with id (the entity id), uuid, name, world, x, y, z, alive, audience, health, max_health, flags, pose
and held_slot. STALE for a gone NPC.

name: hud_npc_item
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_item(int32_t npc, int32_t slot, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: npc_item: what the NPC holds in a Bukkit slot, as a map with item and count. ABSENT when the slot is empty.

name: hud_npc_attribute
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_attribute(int32_t npc, const char *name, int32_t nlen, double *out)
doc:
npc_attribute: the current value of an attribute (a name without namespace means minecraft:), stored in `*out`.
OK; ABSENT when the NPC lacks it.

name: hud_npc_animate
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_animate(int32_t npc, int32_t action)
doc: npc_animate: plays an animation of the ClientboundAnimatePacket action id (0 swing main hand). OK; STALE.

name: hud_npc_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_npc_remove(int32_t npc)
doc: npc_remove: OK; STALE.

name: hud_player_set
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_player_set(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc: player_set: applies the present keys. OK; STALE; INVALID for an unknown key or a value of the wrong type.

name: hud_player_get
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_player_get(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: player_get: a map holding every property above. STALE for a gone player.

name: hud_tab_entry
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_tab_entry(int32_t viewer, int32_t entity_id, int32_t listed)
doc:
tab_entry: whether this viewer's tab list shows the player with the entity id. OK; INVALID when no online player has
that entity id (an NPC is not a tab list entry).

name: hud_surface_claim
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_surface_claim(const char *surface, int32_t slen, int32_t priority, const char *spec, int32_t cslen, int32_t token)
doc:
surface_claim: claims the surface. `spec` is the static content, or empty; `token` is a render callback, 0 for none.
The callback runs per player and redraw with a completion ctx whose value_result is a map with surface and player
(the name, for player_by_name); it answers with surface_answer, and not answering draws nothing for that player.
The claim's handle; INVALID for an unknown surface name.

name: hud_surface_update
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_surface_update(int32_t claim, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc: surface_update: replaces the static content. OK; STALE.

name: hud_surface_release
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_surface_release(int32_t claim)
doc: surface_release: lets go of the surface. OK; STALE.

name: hud_surface_answer
signature: int32_t basalt_hud_surface_answer(int32_t ctx, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
surface_answer: inside a render callback, the content for that player. OK; STALE once the callback returned;
INVALID for a ctx that is not a render callback or a bad spec.

name: inventory_of_player
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_of_player(int32_t player)
doc:
inventory_of_player: the inventory of an online player. Returns a handle, STALE for a player that left, INVALID
for a bad player handle. Never needs a capability.

name: inventory_of_block
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_of_block(const char *world, int32_t wlen, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z)
doc:
inventory_of_block: the container block entity at (x, y, z) of the world named `world` (empty means the default
world). Returns a handle; ABSENT when the world is unknown or the block holds no container, INVALID for bad text.

name: inventory_of_window
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_of_window(int32_t player)
doc:
inventory_of_window: the container window the player has open right now (including their own inventory slots, as
in the protocol). Returns a handle; ABSENT when no window is open or the connection has none (Bedrock), STALE or
INVALID for the player. The handle goes STALE when that window closes.

name: inventory_of_ender
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_of_ender(int32_t player)
doc: inventory_of_ender: the ender chest of an online player (27 slots). Returns a handle, STALE or INVALID for the player.

name: inventory_of_entity
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_of_entity(int32_t entity)
doc:
inventory_of_entity: the inventory of a player entity (`entity` handle of entities.h, from entity_of_player). Returns
a handle; ABSENT when the entity is not a player, STALE for a removed entity, INVALID for a bad handle. The player
operations send_equipment and open_trades and the properties slot_limit and enchantment_seed are reached with
entity_call and entity_get/entity_set on the same entity handle.

name: inventory_release
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_release(int32_t inventory)
doc: inventory_release: forgets the handle. OK, STALE when it was already released, INVALID when malformed.

name: inventory_size
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_size(int32_t inventory)
doc: inventory_size: the number of slots (window: the slots of the whole window). STALE or INVALID for the handle.

name: inventory_get
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_get(int32_t inventory, int32_t slot, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
inventory_get: the stack in `slot` as an item value written to `out` (needed-length convention); an empty slot is
the null value (1 byte). INVALID for a slot out of range, STALE or INVALID for the handle.

name: inventory_set
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_set(int32_t inventory, int32_t slot, const char *item, int32_t ilen)
doc:
inventory_set: puts the item value (or null to empty the slot) in `slot` and resends the inventory to whoever has
it open. OK; INVALID for a bad slot, bad item value or unknown item id, STALE or INVALID for the handle.

name: inventory_add
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_add(int32_t inventory, const char *item, int32_t ilen)
doc:
inventory_add: puts the item value where it fits, merging stacks first. Returns the count that did NOT fit (0 means
all of it went in); negative for INVALID (bad item), STALE or INVALID (handle).

name: inventory_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_remove(int32_t inventory, const char *id, int32_t idlen, int32_t count)
doc:
inventory_remove: takes up to `count` of item `id` (any components). Returns how many were taken (0 when none);
negative for INVALID (count below 1 or empty id), STALE or INVALID (handle).

name: inventory_count
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_count(int32_t inventory, const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc: inventory_count: how many of item `id` the inventory holds in total. Negative for STALE or INVALID.

name: inventory_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_clear(int32_t inventory)
doc: inventory_clear: empties every slot (for a window only the container part). OK, STALE or INVALID.

name: inventory_contents
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_contents(int32_t inventory, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
inventory_contents: every non-empty slot as a list of maps {"slot": int, "item": item value}, in slot order, written
to `out` (needed-length convention). STALE or INVALID for the handle.

name: inventory_held_slot
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_held_slot(int32_t inventory)
doc:
inventory_held_slot: the selected hotbar index 0..8 of a player inventory. ABSENT for any other kind, STALE or
INVALID for the handle.

name: inventory_set_held_slot
signature: int32_t basalt_inventory_set_held_slot(int32_t inventory, int32_t slot)
doc:
inventory_set_held_slot: selects hotbar index 0..8 on a player inventory. OK; INVALID for an index out of range,
ABSENT for another kind, STALE or INVALID for the handle.

name: item_cooldown
signature: int32_t basalt_item_cooldown(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc:
item_cooldown: ticks left on the use cooldown of item `id` for the player, 0 when none. INVALID for empty id,
STALE or INVALID for the player.

name: item_set_cooldown
signature: int32_t basalt_item_set_cooldown(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t idlen, int32_t ticks)
doc:
item_set_cooldown: starts (ticks above 0) or clears (0 or less) the use cooldown of item `id` for the player.
OK; INVALID for empty id, STALE or INVALID for the player.

name: registry_get
signature: int32_t basalt_registry_get(const char *kind, int32_t klen, const char *key, int32_t keylen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
registry_get: reads item related registry data by kind into `out` as a value (needed-length convention).
`kind` is one of (the argument `key` is the text after it):
  "item"           key = item id: map of what the registries know (max_stack_size, max_damage, food, tool rules...)
  "items"          key ignored: list of every item id in registry order
  "creative_tab"   key = tab (`building_blocks`): list of item ids in display order, empty for tabs without a list
  "enchantment"    key = enchantment id: the datapack definition as a map
  "enchantments"   key ignored: list of every enchantment id
  "tags"           key = registry (`enchantment`, `item`...): map of tag id to list of member ids
  "mob_effects"    key ignored: list of maps {id, protocol_id, colour}
  "potions"        key ignored: list of maps {id, effects}
ABSENT when the id of an "item" or "enchantment" is unknown, INVALID for an unknown kind.

name: enchantment_level_value
signature: double basalt_enchantment_level_value(const char *spec, int32_t slen, int32_t level)
doc:
enchantment_level_value: evaluates an enchantment level based number at `level`. `spec` is a value: a bare number,
or a map with "type" (constant, linear, levels_squared, clamped, fraction, exponent, lookup) and that type's
fields as in the datapack format ("value", "base", "per_level_above_first", "added", "min", "max", "numerator",
"denominator", "power", "values", "fallback"). Returns the number; 0.0 for a malformed spec.

name: recipe_add
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_add(const char *id, int32_t idlen, const char *json, int32_t jlen)
doc:
recipe_add: registers a recipe from the datapack recipe JSON text. OK; INVALID when the id is taken, the id is
malformed or the JSON is not a recipe. Types: crafting_shaped, crafting_shapeless, crafting_transmute, smelting,
blasting, smoking, campfire_cooking, stonecutting, smithing_transform, smithing_trim, brewing (input, reagent,
output) and the special crafting recipes.

name: recipe_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_remove(const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc: recipe_remove: takes a recipe, the server's own included, out of every lookup. OK, ABSENT when there is none.

name: recipe_has
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_has(const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc: recipe_has: 1 when a recipe by that id exists, else 0. INVALID for empty id.

name: recipe_ids
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_ids(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: recipe_ids: every recipe id (the datapack's first, then the added ones) as a list of strings (needed-length).

name: recipe_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_clear(void)
doc:
recipe_clear: empties the recipe list. recipe_reset: puts back the datapack recipes and drops the added ones.
recipe_reset_brewing: drops the brewing recipes plugins added and restores the shipped ones. All return OK.

name: recipe_reset
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_reset(void)

name: recipe_reset_brewing
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_reset_brewing(void)

name: recipe_get
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_get(const char *id, int32_t idlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: recipe_get: a recipe as a map mirroring its fields (needed-length). ABSENT when there is none.

name: recipe_station
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_station(const char *kind, int32_t klen, const char *input, int32_t ilen, char *out, int32_t cap)

name: recipe_book_get
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_book_get(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: recipe_book_get: the recipe ids the player has discovered, a list of strings (needed-length).

name: recipe_book_set
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_book_set(int32_t player, const char *ids, int32_t ilen, int32_t learn)
doc:
recipe_book_set: `ids` is a list value of recipe ids; with `learn` 1 they are discovered, with 0 forgotten.
Returns how many actually changed; negative for INVALID (bad list) or STALE/INVALID (player).

name: recipe_book_has
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_book_has(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc: recipe_book_has: 1 when the player knows the recipe, else 0.

name: recipe_book_resend
signature: int32_t basalt_recipe_book_resend(int32_t player)
doc: recipe_book_resend: sends the player the recipe packet and recipe book again. OK; ABSENT when the connection has none.

name: merchant_open
signature: int32_t basalt_merchant_open(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
merchant_open: opens a merchant window with trades the plugin made. `spec` is {"title": MiniMessage string,
"offers": list of {"buy": item, "buy2": item or null, "sell": item, "uses": int, "max_uses": int, "xp": int,
"price_multiplier": float, "demand": int, "special_price": int}}. OK; ABSENT when the connection has no merchant
window, INVALID for a bad spec, STALE or INVALID for the player.

name: window_open
signature: int32_t basalt_window_open(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
window_open: opens a plugin-held container window for the player. `spec` is {"kind": string (chest, barrel,
shulker_box, hopper, dispenser, dropper, furnace, blast_furnace, smoker, brewing_stand, crafter, anvil, grindstone,
loom, cartography_table, stonecutter, smithing, enchanting, beacon, lectern, merchant, crafting),
"size": int (chest only, rounded up to rows of 9, default 27), "title": MiniMessage string, "items": list of item
or null per slot, "editable": bool (default true)}. Returns the container id (positive); INVALID for an unknown
kind or bad spec, ABSENT when the connection has no windows, STALE or INVALID for the player.

name: window_info
signature: int32_t basalt_window_info(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
window_info: the player's open window as {"container_id": int, "kind": string, "slots": int, "plugin": bool,
"world": string, "block": {"x","y","z"} when it belongs to a block} (needed-length). ABSENT when none is open.

name: window_close
signature: int32_t basalt_window_close(int32_t player)
doc: window_close: closes the window the player has open. OK, ABSENT when none.

name: window_update
signature: int32_t basalt_window_update(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
window_update: changes the open window with a map: "title" (MiniMessage string, reopens the screen under the new
title) and "properties" (map of data id as decimal string to int, furnace progress, enchantment costs, anvil
cost). Unknown keys ignored. OK; ABSENT when no window is open or a property is not accepted, INVALID for a bad
map.

name: container_menu_create
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_create(const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
container_menu_create: `spec` is {"title": MiniMessage string, "rows": int 1..6 (chest, default 3), "kind": string
as window_open (default "chest")}. Returns the menu handle; INVALID for a bad spec or unknown kind.

name: container_menu_set
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_set(int32_t menu, int32_t slot, const char *item, int32_t ilen, int32_t token)
doc:
container_menu_set: puts the item value in `slot` of the menu and registers `token` for clicks on it (0 for no
handler); a null item clears the slot and its handler. Redraws for everyone who has the menu open. OK; INVALID for
a slot out of range, a bad item or a bad menu handle.

name: container_menu_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_clear(int32_t menu)
doc: container_menu_clear: removes every item and handler of the menu. OK, INVALID for a bad handle.

name: container_menu_open
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_open(int32_t menu, int32_t player)
doc:
container_menu_open: shows the menu to the player, replacing a window they had open. OK; ABSENT when the connection
has no windows, STALE or INVALID for the player, INVALID for a bad menu.

name: container_menu_close
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_close(int32_t menu, int32_t player)
doc: container_menu_close: closes the menu for that player if they have it open. OK, ABSENT when they do not.

name: container_menu_click_info
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_click_info(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
container_menu_click_info: during a click callback, the click as {"player": int player handle, "slot": int,
"button": int, "mode": string} (needed-length); the server reports button 0 and mode "pickup". STALE or INVALID for ctx.

name: container_menu_click_result
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_click_result(int32_t ctx, const char *item, int32_t ilen)
doc:
container_menu_click_result: replaces the stack shown in the clicked slot with the item value (null clears it);
applied after the callback returns. OK; INVALID for a bad item, STALE or INVALID for ctx.

name: container_menu_click_cancel
signature: int32_t basalt_container_menu_click_cancel(int32_t ctx, int32_t cancelled)
doc:
container_menu_click_cancel: sets whether the click is cancelled. See the note above for what the server accepts.
OK, DENIED when the server cannot honour the value, STALE or INVALID for ctx.

name: loot_tables
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_tables(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: loot_tables: every loot table id as a list of strings (needed-length).

name: loot_roll
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_roll(const char *table, int32_t tlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
loot_roll: what the loot table `table` gives for the roll spec, a list of item values (needed-length). ABSENT when
the table or the world is unknown, INVALID for a bad spec.

name: loot_roll_json
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_roll_json(const char *json, int32_t jlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
loot_roll_json: the same for a loot table given as JSON text (the format of a loot table file). ABSENT when the JSON
does not parse as a table or the world is unknown, INVALID for a bad spec.

name: loot_number
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_number(const char *json, int32_t jlen, int32_t as_float, int64_t seed, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
loot_number: evaluates a number provider given as JSON text with an empty context. `as_float` 1 picks a float
provider, 0 an int one. The answer is a value, an int or a float (needed-length). ABSENT when the JSON does not parse,
INVALID for bad arguments.

name: loot_apply
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_apply(const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
loot_apply: runs loot functions on a stack. `spec` is {"functions": JSON text (one function object or an array),
"item": item value, "world", "x", "y", "z", "seed" optional}. The answer is the resulting item value (needed-length).
ABSENT when the JSON or the world is unknown, INVALID for a bad spec.

name: loot_enchant
signature: int32_t basalt_loot_enchant(const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
loot_enchant: rolls enchantments onto a stack as the enchant_with_levels function does. `spec` is {"item": item
value, "levels": int, "options": enchantment id or a tag with a leading `#` (default `#minecraft:in_enchanting_table`),
"seed", "world" optional}. The answer is the resulting item value (needed-length). ABSENT when the world is unknown,
INVALID for a bad spec.

name: trades_roll
signature: int32_t basalt_trades_roll(const char *profession, int32_t plen, int32_t level, const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
trades_roll: the trades a villager of `profession` offers at `level` (1 to 5), as a list of maps {"cost_a": item,
"cost_b": item or null, "result": item, "max_uses": int, "xp": int, "price_multiplier": float} (needed-length).
`spec` takes the roll keys plus "variant" (villager type), "amount" (int) and "listed" (list of trade ids to draw
from without repeats). ABSENT when the profession, level or world is unknown, INVALID for a bad spec.

name: channel_listen
signature: int32_t basalt_channel_listen(const char *name, int32_t name_len, int32_t token)
doc:
channel_listen: calls `token` for every message a client sends on plugin channel `name` (for example
"example:chan"); ctx answers packet_ctx_info (kind "channel"), packet_ctx_body and packet_ctx_player. The packet_ctx
setters and relays on a channel ctx return BASALT_ERR_INVALID. OK; DENIED without the network capability or for a
channel the manifest does not list; INVALID for an empty name. The listener stays until the plugin is disabled.

name: channel_send
signature: int32_t basalt_channel_send(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t name_len, const char *body, int32_t body_len)
doc:
channel_send: sends `body` to `player` on plugin channel `name`. 1 when it was sent, 0 when the player cannot
receive it (not a Java client, or the client did not register the channel). STALE for a player that left, INVALID
for a bad handle or name, DENIED as above. Owner thread: the plugin's.

name: packet_listen
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_listen(const char *pattern, int32_t pattern_len, const char *options, int32_t options_len, int32_t token)
doc:
packet_listen: calls `token` for every packet that `pattern` matches. `options` is one value (basalt_values.h):
null for the defaults, or a map with the optional keys "priority" (string "first", "early", "normal", "late" or
"last", default "normal"; first runs first) and "observe" (bool, default false). An observer only watches: its
packet_ctx_cancel and packet_ctx_set_body return DENIED and what it did is dropped. A plain listener may cancel the
packet or replace its body; once a listener cancelled a packet, later plain listeners are skipped and observers
still see it; with several replacements the last one wins. The packet ctx answers every packet_ctx_* import.
Returns the listener handle (a positive i32, STALE after packet_unlisten or when the plugin is disabled); INVALID
for an unknown name or bad options; DENIED without the packets capability. With no listener on a packet the server
pays one atomic read for it.

name: packet_unlisten
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_unlisten(int32_t listener)
doc:
packet_unlisten: removes a listener made by packet_listen. OK; STALE for a handle that was already removed;
INVALID for a malformed handle. Allowed from inside the listener itself.

name: packet_send
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_send(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t name_len, const char *body, int32_t body_len, int32_t intercept)
doc:
packet_send: sends the clientbound packet `name` with `body` to `player`. `intercept` non-zero runs the listeners on
it (including this plugin's), zero sends it past them. 1 when written, 0 when the player has no Java connection
(Bedrock) or it is closing; INVALID for an unknown or serverbound name or a bad body; STALE for a player that left;
DENIED without the packets capability. The body is in the wire format of the player's protocol.

name: packet_receive
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_receive(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t name_len, const char *body, int32_t body_len, int32_t intercept)
doc:
packet_receive: handles the serverbound packet `name` as if the player's client had sent it. Same arguments and
results as packet_send, with a serverbound name.

name: packet_lookup
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_lookup(const char *name, int32_t name_len, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_lookup: what `name` means, as one map value written to `out` with the usual needed-length result: "name"
(string, as the server spells it), "phase" (string, null for a wildcard over all phases), "serverbound" (bool, null
when a wildcard covers both), "id" (int, null for a wildcard) and "wildcard" (bool). INVALID for a name this server
does not have, DENIED without the packets capability.

name: packet_names
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_names(const char *prefix, int32_t prefix_len, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_names: the packet names that start with `prefix` (empty for all), as a value list of strings in the order
of `/plugins packets`, written with the needed-length convention. DENIED without the packets capability.

name: packet_player_actions
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_player_actions(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_player_actions: the names accepted by packet_player_receive, as a value list of strings, generated from the
server's own player operation table. DENIED without the packets capability.

name: packet_player_receive
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_player_receive(int32_t player, const char *action, int32_t action_len, const char *args, int32_t args_len)
doc:
packet_player_receive: does what the client packet named `action` would do for `player`: use_item, use_item_on,
container_click, interact, attack, custom_payload, chat_command, move, pick_block, pick_entity, place_recipe,
creative_slot, sign_update, rename_item, beacon, select_trade, container_button, container_close, held_slot, chat,
edit_book (packet_player_actions lists them). `args` is one value: a list of the arguments in the order the server
documents for that action (numbers, booleans, strings, null, a list of strings for book pages). 1 when the server
accepted it, 0 when it did not (no Java connection, or the packet was refused); INVALID for an unknown action or an
argument that is not a scalar or a list of strings; STALE for a player that left; DENIED without the packets
capability.

name: packet_ctx_info
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_info(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_ctx_info: writes one map value describing what the listener is looking at. Packet: "kind" ("packet"),
"name", "phase", "id", "serverbound", "connection" (int, stable for the connection), "protocol" (the version the
client announced, 0 before the handshake), "translated" (bool, the bytes are in the server's shape for an older
client), "size", "player_name", "player_uuid" (empty before login), "cancelled" (what earlier listeners decided) and
"observer". Channel: "kind" ("channel"), "channel", "size", "player_name", "player_uuid". Needed-length result;
STALE once the callback returned, INVALID for another kind of ctx.

name: packet_ctx_body
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_body(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_ctx_body: writes the body as it arrived (not what earlier listeners replaced it with), needed-length result,
STALE or INVALID as packet_ctx_info.

name: packet_ctx_player
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_player(int32_t ctx)
doc:
packet_ctx_player: the handle of the player the packet or message belongs to, 0 when there is none yet (before
login) or the player is gone. STALE or INVALID as packet_ctx_info.

name: packet_ctx_cancel
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_cancel(int32_t ctx)
doc:
packet_ctx_cancel: cancels the packet, so it is neither sent nor handled. OK; DENIED for an observer; INVALID for a
channel ctx; STALE once the callback returned.

name: packet_ctx_set_body
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_set_body(int32_t ctx, const char *body, int32_t body_len)
doc:
packet_ctx_set_body: replaces the body that continues on its way. OK; INVALID for a body over 1 MiB, bad pointers or
a channel ctx; DENIED for an observer; STALE once the callback returned.

name: packet_ctx_send
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_send(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t name_len, const char *body, int32_t body_len, int32_t intercept)
doc:
packet_ctx_send: sends another clientbound packet on the connection this packet travels on (pkt:send). Arguments and
results as packet_send without the player; INVALID for a channel ctx, 0 when the connection is gone.

name: packet_ctx_receive
signature: int32_t basalt_packet_ctx_receive(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t name_len, const char *body, int32_t body_len, int32_t intercept)
doc:
packet_ctx_receive: hands a serverbound packet to the server as if the client had sent it on this connection
(pkt:receive). Arguments and results as packet_ctx_send with a serverbound name.

name: servers_register
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_servers_register(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *host, int32_t hlen, int32_t port, const char *like, int32_t llen, char *err, int32_t ecap)
doc:
servers_register: adds a backend `name` at host:port (1..65535) until the proxy stops, copying the settings (forwarding,
timeouts, protocol range) of the backend `like` ("" copies none). The names listed in basalt_proxy_servers_list are the
proxy's own, so register only a name that is not there. Returns OK, or INVALID with the reason (UTF-8, truncated to
`ecap`, not NUL terminated, the byte count is not returned) written to `err` when `ecap` is positive.

name: servers_unregister
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_servers_unregister(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
servers_unregister: removes a backend added by servers_register. OK; ABSENT when no backend has that name; DENIED when
it is one of servers.toml, which a plugin may not remove.

name: servers_ping
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_servers_ping(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t token)
doc:
servers_ping: asks backend `name` for its server list status. Returns a request handle (core_values.h); later
basalt_callback(token, ctx) runs on the plugin thread and basalt_value_result gives a map with motd (plain text),
motd_json (string), online, max_players, protocol, latency (ints, latency in ms) and version (string), or null when
the backend did not answer. ABSENT when the backend does not exist or the ping cannot start, INVALID for a bad name,
INVALID when too many requests are pending. Cancel with basalt_request_cancel.

name: console_run
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_console_run(const char *line, int32_t len)
doc:
console_run: runs `line` (no slash, at most 4096 bytes) as the console would and logs "ran /line" under the plugin. 1
when the line named a command, 0 when it did not; DENIED without the commands capability and the operator's grant.
It reaches the commands that plugins registered and the proxy's own; the answer of the command goes to the log.

name: player_chat
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_chat(int32_t player, const char *text, int32_t len)
doc:
player_chat: makes the player say `text` (cut at 256 bytes), or run it as a command when it starts with '/'; unsigned, so
the proxy and the backend see a message the client did not sign. OK once handed over, INVALID for an empty text or when
the player's connection cannot take it, STALE for a player that left.

name: permission_check
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_check(const char *who, int32_t wlen, const char *node, int32_t nlen, const char *context, int32_t clen)
doc:
permission_check: asks the chain whether `who` has `node`. `who` is a player name, exact spelling first and then
ignoring case, or "" for the console; a player that is not connected is asked by name alone. `context` is an optional
map (length 0 for none): server and world (strings, the server defaults to the player's backend) and any number of other
string entries that providers read. Returns 1 granted, 0 denied, ABSENT when nothing in the chain decided (the proxy
counts that as denied). INVALID for a context that is not a map of strings.

name: permission_meta
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_meta(const char *who, int32_t wlen, const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *context, int32_t clen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
permission_meta: the text option `key` (prefix, suffix or any other) of `who`, same naming and context as
permission_check. Writes the text to `out`; returns the length the full answer needs, written only when it fits in
`cap`; ABSENT when nothing provides it.

name: permission_provide
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_provide(int32_t check_token, int32_t meta_token, int32_t priority)
doc:
permission_provide: puts a provider in the chain. `check_token` (0 for none) is called as basalt_callback(token, ctx)
to answer a check, `meta_token` (0 for none) to answer a meta question; at least one is needed. `priority` is above the
proxy's default provider and decides the order among plugins, highest first; 0 means the plugin default (100).
Returns the provider handle (positive i32), INVALID when both tokens are 0 or the priority is negative, ABSENT when
the proxy has no permission chain. The provider goes away with permission_unprovide or when the plugin is disabled.

name: permission_unprovide
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_unprovide(int32_t provider)
doc: permission_unprovide: takes the provider out of the chain. OK, or STALE for a handle already removed.

name: permission_request
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_request(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
permission_request: inside a provider callback, writes a map describing the question: kind ("check" or "meta"), name,
uuid (strings, uuid is "" when unknown), console (bool), text (the node of a check, the key of a meta) and context (a
map with server, world and any extra string entries). Needed-length convention. STALE after the callback or when the
asker stopped waiting, INVALID when ctx is not a provider question.

name: permission_answer
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_answer(int32_t ctx, int32_t answer)
doc:
permission_answer: answers a check question: 1 grants, 0 denies, any negative value leaves it undefined (the next
provider decides). The last call before the callback returns counts. OK, INVALID when ctx is a meta question or not a
provider question, STALE when the answer is late.

name: permission_answer_text
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_answer_text(int32_t ctx, const char *text, int32_t len)
doc:
permission_answer_text: answers a meta question with `text` (up to 4096 bytes). Same results as permission_answer;
a call with a negative length leaves the answer undefined.

name: permission_changed
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_changed(void)
doc:
permission_changed: tells the proxy that what the providers answer changed, so it rebuilds what it derived from them.
OK; ABSENT when the proxy has no permission chain.

name: permission_override
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_override(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *node, int32_t olen, int32_t value)
doc:
permission_override: grants (1), denies (0) or removes (-1) `node` for the player named `name` (connected or not)
until the proxy stops; the override is asked before the groups. OK, INVALID for another value or an empty node.

name: permission_list
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_permission_list(const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
permission_list: writes the nodes the player named `name` has right now (groups and overrides) as a value list of
strings, sorted. Needed-length convention.

name: group_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_group_get(const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: group_get: writes the name of the player's group, "" in length when none. Needed-length convention.

name: group_set
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_group_set(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *group, int32_t glen)
doc:
group_set: puts the player named `name` in `group`; an empty group clears it. OK, INVALID when the player never
joined the proxy or the group is not defined in groups.toml.

name: player_send_json
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_send_json(int32_t player, const char *json, int32_t len)
doc:
player_send_json: sends a chat line given as a text component in JSON (at most 65536 bytes). OK, STALE for a player
that left, INVALID when the text is not a valid component.

name: player_kick_json
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_kick_json(int32_t player, const char *json, int32_t len)
doc: player_kick_json: disconnects the player with a reason given as component JSON. Results as player_send_json.

name: store_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_store_get(const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
store_get: writes the value of `key` in the plugin's own store (shared by every player and kept in the proxy's plugin
database), a bool, int, float or string value (the encoding of basalt_values.h). A float without a fraction reads back
as an int. Needed-length convention. ABSENT when the key is not set, DENIED without the storage capability, INVALID
for an empty key or one over 128 bytes or when the proxy has no plugin database.

name: store_set
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_store_set(const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
store_set: sets `key` to the encoded value (value, vlen), a bool, int, float or string of at most 65536 bytes; a null
value deletes the key. A plugin may hold 1000 keys here. OK, DENIED, INVALID for a key as above, another type, an
oversized value or the 1001st key.

name: store_top
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_store_top(const char *key, int32_t klen, int32_t limit, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
store_top: the best `limit` (1..1000, default 10 for a value under 1) numeric values of `key` across the plugin's store
and the data of every player, highest first, as a list of maps with uuid ("server" for the store), name (the player's
name when connected, else the uuid) and value (int or float). Rows whose value is not a number are skipped. Needed-length
convention; DENIED without the storage capability, INVALID as store_get.

name: player_data_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_data_get(const char *holder, int32_t hlen, const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_data_get: reads `key` of the plugin's data for the holder, the player's UUID text as the proxy knows it (a
player that never reported one is held by name), whether the player is connected or not. Same value encoding, results
and key limits as store_get, with the capability players_data.

name: player_data_set
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_data_set(const char *holder, int32_t hlen, const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
player_data_set: writes or, with a null value, deletes `key` for the holder. Same results as store_set, with a
limit of 1000 keys per holder and plugin.

name: wait
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_wait(int32_t ticks, int32_t token)
doc:
wait: returns a request handle whose completion callback basalt_callback(token, ctx) runs after `ticks` ticks of 50 ms
(0 is one tick) with a null value_result. INVALID for negative ticks or when too many requests are pending; cancel with
basalt_request_cancel.

name: event_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_event_get(int32_t ctx, const char *field, int32_t flen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
event_get: writes into `out` the value of `field` in ctx (the encoding of basalt_values.h) and returns the length the
full answer needs, written only when it fits in `cap`. An empty field name answers a map of every field the event
has right now (write only fields are left out). ABSENT when the event does not have the field, STALE once the
callback returned, INVALID for a live ctx that is not an event (a command) or a field that is not valid text.

name: event_set
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_event_set(int32_t ctx, const char *field, int32_t flen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
event_set: sets `field` of a decided event to the encoded value (value, vlen). OK, STALE for a dead ctx, ABSENT for
a field the event does not have (INVALID for a ctx that is not an event), INVALID when the event is observed, the field is read only, the value has another
type than the field (a bool accepts true or false only, an int an integer, a string a string, sample a list of strings),
the text is over 4096 bytes, a server is not a backend, or a ping number is negative. Setting reason or reason_json
replaces the other, so the last one set wins. Text fields set to null are INVALID.

name: event_fields
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_event_fields(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
event_fields: writes a list of maps, one per field of ctx, with the keys name (string), type ("string", "int", "bool",
"list"), readable (bool) and writable (bool; false on an observed event). Same needed-length convention and errors as
event_get. The table behind it is the one event_get and event_set check against, so it is always complete.

name: event_watch
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_event_watch(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t token)
doc:
event_watch: registers `token` to run basalt_callback(token, ctx) once per finished event named `name` (join, quit,
server_change, chat, kick). Observers run in registration order after the proxy acted and the ctx is read only.
OK, INVALID for an unknown name or one that cannot be observed (login, server_pre_connect, command, ping, plugin.*,
which are decided or lifecycle events). Queued like the other observed events: a full queue drops the event.

name: plugin_info
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_plugin_info(const char *field, int32_t flen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
plugin_info: writes the UTF-8 text of `field`, one of "id", "name" (the id when plugin.toml has none) or "version",
and returns the length the full answer needs, written only when it fits in `cap`. INVALID for another field.

name: plugin_manifest
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_plugin_manifest(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
plugin_manifest: writes a map with id, name, version (strings), authors (list of strings), capabilities (list of the
names declared in plugin.toml) and depends (list of maps with id, requirement and hard) as read from plugin.toml.
Needed-length convention; never fails except INVALID when the document cannot be built.

name: config_value
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_config_value(const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
config_value: writes the value at `key` of config.toml (dots walk nested tables, an empty key is the whole file) as a
value: strings, integers, floats, booleans, lists and maps, with TOML arrays as lists and tables as maps. The file
limits.toml next to config.toml, when present, is readable under the key "limits". ABSENT when the key does not exist;
dashed keys are also found with underscores. Needed-length convention.

name: command_arg_f64
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_command_arg_f64(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t nlen, double *out)
doc:
command_arg_f64: reads the float argument `name` of the command being run (an int argument converts). OK, ABSENT for
an omitted optional or unknown name, INVALID when the argument is not a number, STALE outside a command callback.

name: command_arg_bool
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_command_arg_bool(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t *out)
doc: command_arg_bool: reads the bool argument `name` (the words true and false) into *out as 0 or 1. Results as above.

name: command_args
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_command_args(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
command_args: writes a map with every declared argument of the running command, null for an omitted optional one,
with typed values (string, int, float, bool). Needed-length convention; STALE outside a command callback.

name: hud_clear_title
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_clear_title(int32_t player, int32_t reset)
doc:
hud_clear_title: takes the title, subtitle and action bar off the player's screen; `reset` non zero also puts the
fade times back to their defaults. OK, STALE, ABSENT as above.

name: hud_tab_list
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_tab_list(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
hud_tab_list: sets the header and footer of the player's tab list. `spec` is a map with the optional string keys
header and footer and the optional map args; a missing or null part keeps what the player has, an empty string
clears it. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a spec that is not a map or a part that is not a string.

name: hud_bossbar_show
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_bossbar_show(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
hud_bossbar_show: shows (or replaces) the boss bar `id`. `spec` is a map with the string text (required), the number
progress (default 1.0), the strings color (default "purple") and overlay (default "progress"), and the optional map
args. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for an id that is empty or over 64 bytes, a spec without text or with a key of the
wrong type, or a progress that is not a number.

name: hud_bossbar_hide
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_bossbar_hide(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen)
doc: hud_bossbar_hide: removes the boss bar `id`. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a bad id.

name: hud_bossbar_progress
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_bossbar_progress(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen, double progress)
doc:
hud_bossbar_progress: sets the fill of the boss bar `id` (0 empty, 1 full, clamped). Same results as hud_bossbar_show;
INVALID also for NaN.

name: hud_bossbar_title
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_bossbar_title(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen, const char *text, int32_t tlen, const char *args, int32_t alen)
doc: hud_bossbar_title: sets the text of the boss bar `id`; `args` is the packed list of basalt_abi.h. Same results.

name: hud_bossbar_style
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_bossbar_style(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen, const char *color, int32_t clen, const char *overlay, int32_t olen)
doc:
hud_bossbar_style: sets the color and the overlay of the boss bar `id` by name (see the lists above). Same
results.

name: hud_sidebar
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_sidebar(int32_t player, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
hud_sidebar: shows the plugin's sidebar. `spec` is a map with the string title (required), the list of strings
