lines, top to bottom (at most 15, the rest is ignored), and the optional map args. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a
spec without title or with a line that is not a string.

name: hud_sidebar_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_sidebar_clear(int32_t player)
doc: hud_sidebar_clear: takes the sidebar down. OK, STALE, ABSENT.

name: hud_tab_entry
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_tab_entry(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
hud_tab_entry: adds or updates the fake row `id` in the player's own tab list. `spec` is a map with the strings name
(the profile name of the row) and text (the display text), both required, the integer latency in milliseconds (0 to
10000, clamped, default 0), and the optional map args. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a bad id or spec.

name: hud_tab_entry_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_tab_entry_remove(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t ilen)
doc: hud_tab_entry_remove: removes the fake row `id`. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a bad id.

name: hud_server_links
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_server_links(int32_t player, const char *links, int32_t llen)
doc:
hud_server_links: replaces the links of the client's pause menu. `links` is a list whose items are pairs, either a
map with the strings label and url or a list of two strings [label, url]. A label equal to one of report_bug,
community_guidelines, support, status, feedback, community, website, forums, news or announcements uses that
known link type; any other label is MiniMessage. An empty list clears the links. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for a
value that is not a list of pairs.

name: hud_chat_completions
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_hud_chat_completions(int32_t player, const char *action, int32_t alen, const char *words, int32_t wlen)
doc:
hud_chat_completions: changes the words the client offers when completing chat. `action` is "add", "remove" or
"set" (replace the whole list); `words` is a list of strings. OK, STALE, ABSENT, INVALID for another action or a
value that is not a list of strings.

name: interaction_watch
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_interaction_watch(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t token)
doc:
interaction_watch: registers `token` to run basalt_callback(token, ctx) once per event named `name`
("player.resource_pack" or "player.settings"). OK, INVALID for another name. ctx answers basalt_value_result with the
map above and is STALE once the callback returned. A full proxy queue drops the event like the other observed
events; the proxy keeps no history for plugins that register late.

name: dialog_show
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_dialog_show(int32_t player, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
dialog_show: opens a dialog on the player's screen from one value, a map with:
  kind                 string, "notice" (default), "confirmation" or "multi_action"
  title                string, MiniMessage
  body                 string or list of strings (at most 32 lines, MiniMessage), optional
  buttons              list of maps {label (string, MiniMessage), command (string, at most 256 bytes)}, at most 16
                       entries; a button runs its command as the player when clicked, there is no callback
  can_close_with_escape  bool, default true
Unknown keys are ignored. OK once handed over; STALE for a player who left; INVALID for a value that is not a map, a
kind that is none of the three, a title that is not a string, a body or button of another shape, or a refused
request.

name: dialog_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_dialog_clear(int32_t player)
doc: dialog_clear: closes any dialog the proxy showed. OK, STALE, INVALID when it could not be handed over.

name: resource_pack_push
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_resource_pack_push(int32_t player, const char *value, int32_t vlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
resource_pack_push: offers a pack to the player. `value` is a map with url (string, required), hash (string, the
SHA-1 as 40 hex digits or empty), required (bool, default false), prompt (string MiniMessage, optional) and id
(string: a UUID, or any other text that becomes the name-based UUID of "basalt:resource_pack:<text>"; the default is
the url). The pack id as UUID text is written to `out` with the needed-length convention (the status of the call
when it fails: STALE for a player who left, INVALID for a missing url, a hash that is not 40 hex digits, a bad value
or a refused request). The client answers with player.resource_pack events carrying that id.

name: resource_pack_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_resource_pack_remove(int32_t player, const char *id, int32_t idlen)
doc:
resource_pack_remove: pops one pack by id (the same id rule: UUID text, or text hashed to a UUID). OK, STALE,
INVALID when the request was refused.

name: resource_pack_clear
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_resource_pack_clear(int32_t player)
doc: resource_pack_clear: removes every pack the proxy pushed. OK, STALE, INVALID when refused.

name: cookie_set
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_cookie_set(int32_t player, const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *data, int32_t dlen)
doc:
cookie_set: stores `data` (arbitrary bytes, at most 5120) under the cookie key (an identifier such as
"plugin:session", at most 256 bytes) in the client for its next connection. OK, STALE, INVALID for an empty or over
long key or data over the limit, or a refused request.

name: cookie_request
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_cookie_request(int32_t player, const char *key, int32_t klen, int32_t token)
doc:
cookie_request: asks the client for the cookie `key`. Returns a request handle (positive) and later calls
basalt_callback(token, ctx), whose basalt_value_result is the cookie as bytes, or null when the client has none or
never answered within the proxy's wait. The handle is STALE after the callback and can be dropped with
basalt_request_cancel. Errors: STALE for a player who left, INVALID for an empty key or a refused request, and
ABSENT when too many requests of the plugin are pending.

name: player_transfer
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_transfer(int32_t player, const char *host, int32_t hlen, int32_t port)
doc:
player_transfer: tells the client to reconnect to host:port (the transfer packet; port 1..65535, 25565 is the
usual one). OK, STALE, INVALID for an empty host, a port out of range or a refused request.

name: players_by_uuid
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_players_by_uuid(const char *uuid, int32_t ulen)
doc: players_by_uuid: the handle of the connected player with that UUID text (dashes as the proxy prints it), 0 when none.

name: players_count
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_players_count(const char *server, int32_t slen)
doc:
players_count: how many players are connected to the proxy, or to the backend `server` when it is not empty (0 for a
name that is not a backend). Never fails.

name: players_broadcast
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_players_broadcast(const char *text, int32_t tlen, const char *args, int32_t alen)
doc:
players_broadcast: sends one chat line to every connected player. `text` is MiniMessage or '@' lang key and `args` the
packed arguments list of basalt_abi.h. OK, INVALID for a text that cannot be resolved.

name: player_address
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_address(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_address: writes the client's IP text and returns the length the full answer needs, written only when it
fits. STALE for a player who left, ABSENT when the proxy has no address for them.

name: player_port
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_port(int32_t player)
doc: player_port: the client's source port, STALE for a player who left, ABSENT when unknown.

name: player_settings
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_settings(int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
player_settings: writes the client information as a map (locale string, view_distance int, chat_mode "full",
"system" or "hidden", chat_colors bool, skin_parts int, main_hand "left" or "right", text_filtering bool,
server_listing bool, particles "all", "decreased" or "minimal"), the needed-length convention. ABSENT until the
client has sent it, STALE for a player who left.

name: player_data_get_f64
signature: double basalt_proxy_player_data_get_f64(int32_t player, const char *key, int32_t klen, double def)
doc:
player_data_get_f64: the float stored under `key` in the plugin data of the player (capability players_data), or
`def` when the key is missing, holds another type, the capability is missing or the player left. An integer stored
by basalt_data_set_i64 reads back as that number.

name: player_data_set_f64
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_player_data_set_f64(int32_t player, const char *key, int32_t klen, double value)
doc:
player_data_set_f64: stores a float under `key`. OK, STALE, INVALID for a non finite number or a bad key, DENIED
without the capability players_data. The same key space and limits as basalt_data_set_i64.

name: network_channel_register
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_network_channel_register(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
network_channel_register: wants messages on `name` and announces it to backends. OK (registering twice is OK),
INVALID for a malformed name, one of the BungeeCord channels, or a plugin that already has 64, DENIED without the
network capability.

name: network_channel_unregister
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_network_channel_unregister(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
network_channel_unregister: the plugin stops wanting `name`; the channel stays announced while another plugin
still wants it. OK, ABSENT when this plugin had not registered it, DENIED without the network capability.

name: network_message_on
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_network_message_on(const char *filter, int32_t flen, int32_t token)
doc:
network_message_on: registers `token` to run basalt_callback(token, ctx) for every message the proxy relays on a
channel this plugin registered. `filter` selects one channel (compared exactly) and an empty filter (flen 0) takes
all of the plugin's channels. The callback is observed only: the message was already relayed. ctx answers
network_message_get and basalt_event_player (the player the message belongs to). OK, INVALID for a malformed filter
or a token registered 64 times, DENIED without the network capability.

name: network_message_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_network_message_get(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
network_message_get: inside a network_message_on callback writes a map: player_name (string), player_uuid (string),
channel (string), data (bytes, the whole payload), source ("backend" when a backend sent it toward the client,
"client" when the client sent it toward the backend), server (string, the backend of the player). Needed-length
convention. STALE once the callback returned, INVALID for a ctx that is not a message.

name: network_message_send
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_network_message_send(int32_t player, const char *channel, int32_t clen, const char *data, int32_t dlen, int32_t toward_client)
doc:
network_message_send: sends `data` (up to 32768 bytes, either way) on `channel` for the player handle. toward_client 0 sends it to the player's current backend as if the proxy had written it, 1 to
the player's client. OK once handed over, ABSENT when the proxy could not hand it over (the player is not in play),
STALE for a handle of a player who left, INVALID for a bad channel, a payload over the limit, a toward_client other
than 0 or 1, or a BungeeCord channel, DENIED without the network capability. The data is not interpreted.

name: packet_resolve
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_resolve(const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_resolve: writes a map for one packet name (never a pattern): name (the canonical spelling), serverbound
(bool), phase (string), id (int). Needed-length convention. ABSENT when this proxy has no such packet.

name: packet_names
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_names(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_names: writes a list of every packet name the proxy knows, strings in canonical spelling. Needed-length
convention.

name: packet_on
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_on(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *opts, int32_t olen, int32_t token)
doc:
packet_on: registers a decider listener, `token` runs basalt_callback(token, ctx) for every packet matching `name`
(a name or pattern) before it is relayed, in priority order across plugins. `opts` is an optional value (olen 0 for
none) with the keys priority (string "first", "early", "normal", "late", "last", or int 0..4 with 0 running
first, default normal) and fail ("open" or "closed", default "open"); unknown keys are ignored. Returns a positive
listener handle. INVALID for an unknown name, a malformed opts or a wrong value, DENIED without the packets
capability, ABSENT when this proxy does not relay packets to plugins.

name: packet_watch
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_watch(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *opts, int32_t olen, int32_t token)
doc:
packet_watch: the same as packet_on for an observer: it sees the final packet, after deciders, and its
packet_cancel and packet_set_body answer INVALID. The handle space is shared with packet_on.

name: packet_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_remove(int32_t listener)
doc:
packet_remove: stops a listener. OK, ABSENT for a handle that was already removed. After it returns the token is
never called again for packets that arrive later; a delivery in flight on another thread may still finish.

name: packet_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_get(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_get: inside a packet callback writes a map describing the packet: name, serverbound (bool), phase, id (int),
connection (int, the proxy's id of the connection), protocol (int, the client's), backend_protocol (int, the
backend's, 0 when unknown), translated (bool, the client is older than the proxy speaks natively so the bytes have
the proxy's shape), size (int, body bytes), backend (string, the backend carrying the packet, empty before one),
player_name, player_uuid (strings, empty before login), editable (bool, false for packets the proxy answers itself
and for login packets), observer (bool, the listener was registered with packet_watch), cancelled (bool, a decider
cancelled it; only observers see true). Needed-length convention. STALE once the callback returned, INVALID for a
ctx that is not a packet. basalt_event_player(ctx) answers the player handle (0 before login).

name: packet_body
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_body(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
packet_body: writes the body of the packet (bytes, the replaced body once packet_set_body ran) and returns the
length the full answer needs, written only when it fits in `cap`. Raw bytes, not a value. STALE, INVALID as
packet_get.

name: packet_set_body
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_set_body(int32_t ctx, const char *body, int32_t len)
doc:
packet_set_body: replaces the body that is relayed with (body, len), up to the size limit. OK, STALE, INVALID for a
ctx that is not a packet, an observer, a packet that is not editable, or a body over the limit.

name: packet_cancel
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_cancel(int32_t ctx)
doc:
packet_cancel: drops the packet instead of relaying it. Later deciders are not called for a cancelled packet, only
observers, which see cancelled true. OK, STALE, INVALID as packet_set_body.

name: packet_inject
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_inject(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *body, int32_t len, int32_t intercept)
doc:
packet_inject: sends another packet on the connection of ctx, in the same phase: a clientbound name goes to the
client, a serverbound name is handled as if the client had sent it. `intercept` 1 lets listeners see it. At most 64
packets per callback. OK once handed over, ABSENT when the connection cannot take it, STALE, INVALID for a name
that is not a packet, a phase other than the connection's, a body over the limit or more than 64 injected.

name: packet_send
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_send(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *body, int32_t len)
doc:
packet_send: sends a clientbound packet to the player's client (handle from basalt_player_by_name and the like). OK
once handed over, ABSENT when the player cannot take it now, STALE for a handle of a player who left, INVALID for a
name that is not a clientbound packet or a body over the limit, DENIED without the packets capability.

name: packet_receive
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_packet_receive(int32_t player, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *body, int32_t len)
doc:
packet_receive: makes the proxy handle a serverbound packet as if the player's client had sent it. Results as
packet_send, INVALID for a name that is not a serverbound packet.

name: antibot_verify
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_verify(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
antibot_verify / antibot_unverify: marks or unmarks a player name as verified, so it passes the antibot checks (the
same list the limbo fills). OK, INVALID for a name that is not a valid login name, DENIED without the capability.

name: antibot_unverify
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_unverify(const char *name, int32_t nlen)

name: antibot_is_verified
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_is_verified(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: antibot_is_verified: 1 when the name is on the verified list, 0 when not. INVALID, DENIED as above.

name: antibot_ban
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_ban(const char *address, int32_t alen)
doc:
antibot_ban / antibot_unban: bans or lifts the ban of an IP address text (v4 or v6, no port). OK when the origin of
the address was banned or cleared, ABSENT when an unban found nothing tracked, INVALID for text that is not an
address, DENIED without the capability.

name: antibot_unban
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_unban(const char *address, int32_t alen)

name: antibot_under_attack
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_under_attack(void)
doc: antibot_under_attack: 1 while the antibot is in attack mode, else 0. DENIED without the capability.

name: antibot_on
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_on(int32_t token)
doc:
antibot_on: registers `token` for every antibot event (a verification result, a ban, a mitigation step). Observed
only, on the plugin thread; ctx answers antibot_event_get. OK, INVALID for a token registered 64 times, DENIED
without the capability.

name: antibot_event_get
signature: int32_t basalt_proxy_antibot_event_get(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
antibot_event_get: inside an antibot_on callback writes a map: kind (string), player_name (string), action (string),
reason (string), skipped (int, connections the event stands for, 0 when it is about one), origin (string, the
address or network the event came from). Needed-length convention. STALE, INVALID as network_message_get.

name: permission_check
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_check(const char *subject, int32_t slen, const char *node, int32_t nlen)
doc:
permission_check: asks the whole chain. 1 granted, 0 denied, ABSENT when no provider decides because the subject is
not online (the console always decides), INVALID for an empty node or malformed text. The caller's own provider is
not asked: a plugin never answers its own question through the chain.

name: permission_meta
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_meta(const char *subject, int32_t slen, const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
permission_meta: a text option for a subject from the providers, such as "prefix" or "suffix". Writes it to `out`
and returns the length the full answer needs; ABSENT when no provider gives one or the subject is not online.

name: permission_has
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_has(int32_t player, const char *node, int32_t nlen)
doc:
permission_has: whether the chain grants the online player the node (the player's own may() answer). 1 or 0, STALE
for a player that left, INVALID for an empty node.

name: permission_set
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_set(int32_t player, const char *node, int32_t nlen, int32_t mode)
doc:
permission_set: grants (mode 1), denies (mode 0) or drops this plugin's grant or denial (mode -1) of a node for the
player, on top of the player's group, until the player leaves. The source of the entry is the calling plugin. The
player's command tree is sent again. OK, STALE, INVALID for another mode or an empty node.

name: permission_provide
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_provide(int32_t priority, int32_t kinds, int32_t token)
doc:
permission_provide: answers permission checks for the whole server until the plugin unloads or the provider is
removed. `priority` is above 0, higher asks first (INVALID otherwise); `kinds` is a bit set, 1 for checks and 2 for
options (INVALID when 0). Returns a provider handle. The callback runs with a completion-kind ctx whose value_result
is the query map {kind: "check" or "meta", name: text, uuid: text (empty for the console), console: bool, node:
text (the option key for kind "meta"), world: text (empty when not in a world)}. A check answers with
permission_answer, an option with permission_answer_meta; not answering lets lower providers decide. The callback is
a decision: it must answer inside the call, and a query raised on another thread, or while this plugin is inside any
other callback, is skipped as undecided.

name: permission_provider_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_provider_remove(int32_t provider)
doc: permission_provider_remove: stops a provider. OK, or ABSENT for an unknown or already removed handle.

name: permission_answer
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_answer(int32_t ctx, int32_t answer)
doc:
permission_answer: inside a "check" provider callback, answer 1 (granted), 0 (denied) or -1 (undecided). OK, STALE
once the callback returned, INVALID for another ctx, another kind of query or another answer.

name: permission_answer_meta
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_answer_meta(int32_t ctx, const char *text, int32_t len)
doc: permission_answer_meta: inside a "meta" provider callback, answers the option with text. OK, STALE, INVALID.

name: permission_changed
signature: int32_t basalt_permission_changed(void)
doc: permission_changed: says the answers of this plugin's providers changed, so command trees are sent again. OK.

name: command_register_ex
signature: int32_t basalt_command_register_ex(const char *spec, int32_t slen, const char *permission, int32_t plen, int32_t token, int32_t complete_token)
doc:
command_register_ex: like command_register and also lets the plugin change the command later: only a command
registered through this import can be aliased or unregistered. A non-negative `complete_token` also asks the
plugin for tab completions of the command's arguments: that callback runs with a command-kind ctx (command_source
and command_arg_* work) and command_complete_input gives the text typed so far for the current argument; the
callback adds candidates with command_complete_add. It runs on the thread that handles tab completion, only when
that is the plugin thread (otherwise nothing is offered) and never while the plugin is in another callback. A
negative `complete_token` means no completions. OK, INVALID for a malformed or already registered spec.

name: command_complete_input
signature: int32_t basalt_command_complete_input(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
command_complete_input: inside a completion callback, writes the text typed so far for the current argument and
returns the length the full answer needs. INVALID outside a completion callback, STALE after it.

name: command_complete_add
signature: int32_t basalt_command_complete_add(int32_t ctx, const char *text, int32_t len)
doc:
command_complete_add: inside a completion callback, offers one candidate replacement for the current argument.
OK, or INVALID for an empty text or a ctx that is not a completion callback.

name: command_alias
signature: int32_t basalt_command_alias(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *alias, int32_t alen)
doc:
command_alias: registers `alias` as another first word for every command this plugin registered through
command_register_ex under `name`, with the same arguments, handlers and permission (the permission of the original
name when none was given). OK, ABSENT when the plugin has no command called `name`, INVALID when
`alias` is empty, has a space, or is already a command of this plugin.

name: command_unregister
signature: int32_t basalt_command_unregister(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
command_unregister: removes every command_register_ex command (and alias) of this plugin under the first word
`name`; the result is how many were removed, ABSENT for none. It works at any time, so a plugin can change its
command set while the server runs.

name: command_run
signature: int32_t basalt_command_run(const char *command, int32_t clen, int32_t player)
doc:
command_run: queues a command line (a leading slash is optional) to run as the console (player 0) or as the player
on the next tick, after the current callback returned, so the command may call back into the plugin without nesting.
Both need capability `commands`. 1 when it was queued, DENIED without the capability, STALE for a player that left,
INVALID for an empty line.

name: command_arg_f64
signature: int32_t basalt_command_arg_f64(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t nlen, double *out)
doc:
command_arg_f64: the float argument `name` of the command ctx, converting an integer. ABSENT when it was not typed,
INVALID when it is not numeric. Writes the value at `out`.

name: command_arg_bool
signature: int32_t basalt_command_arg_bool(int32_t ctx, const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t *out)
doc:
command_arg_bool: the bool argument `name`, 1 or 0 at `out`. ABSENT when it was not typed, INVALID when it is not
a bool argument.

name: command_source
signature: int32_t basalt_command_source(int32_t ctx, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
command_source: describes who ran the command, as a value map {name: text, console: bool, kind: "console",
"player", "command_block", "proxied" or "other", world: text, x: f64, y: f64, z: f64, caller: text (for a proxied
call, the sender that asked: its kind, a colon and its name)}. Length the full answer needs, STALE, INVALID.

name: command_source_player
signature: int32_t basalt_command_source_player(int32_t ctx)
doc:
command_source_player: the player handle of the sender of a command ctx, 0 when it is the console or not a player
who is online. STALE, INVALID.

name: server_broadcast
signature: int32_t basalt_server_broadcast(const char *text, int32_t tlen, const char *args, int32_t alen, int32_t flags)
doc:
server_broadcast: sends `text` (a '@' prefix is a lang key, anything else MiniMessage; arguments as in
player_send) to the audience of `flags`: bit 1 every online player, bit 2 the console log of the plugin. Returns the
number of players it reached (0 when only the console was asked). ABSENT for an unknown lang key, INVALID for no
bit or malformed arguments.

name: placeholder_fill
signature: int32_t basalt_placeholder_fill(const char *text, int32_t tlen, int32_t player, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
placeholder_fill: replaces every "%name%" of `text` with the registered placeholders' answers for the player (0 for
none), into `out`; length the full answer needs. STALE for a player that left.

name: server_info
signature: int32_t basalt_server_info(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
server_info: a value map {software: "Basalt", version: text (empty when unknown), minecraft: text, protocol: i64,
tps_1m: f64, tps_5m: f64, tps_15m: f64, mean_tick_ms: f64, tick_rate: f64, frozen: bool, paused: bool,
online: i64, max_players: i64 (0 when unknown), plugins: [{id, name, version, disabled}], plugin: {id, name,
version, authors: [text], lane: 0, lanes: 1, folder: text}}. Length the full answer needs.

name: server_call
signature: int32_t basalt_server_call(const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
server_call: the administrative operations, by name, with one value in and one value out (`args` may be empty with
alen 0). Unknown operation or malformed arguments is INVALID; the result is the length the full answer needs. The
operations and their arguments (a map unless said) and results:
  settings.keys                          list of text
  settings.get {key}                     text, null when unknown
  settings.set {key, value}              bool (false when read only or the value does not fit)
  tick.rate | tick.set_rate {rate}       f64 | null
  tick.frozen | tick.set_frozen {frozen} bool | null
  tick.step {count} | tick.sprint {count}    bool
  tick.stop_sprint                       bool
  tick.pace                              {tps_1m, tps_5m, tps_15m, mean_tick_ms}
  tick.times                             list of i64 nanoseconds (the last hundred ticks)
  tick.paused                            bool
  links.list                             list of {kind, label, url}
  links.set {links: list of {kind, label, url}}    null
  access.is_banned | is_whitelisted | is_operator {who}    bool (who: uuid or name)
  access.known {who}                     {uuid, name, first_seen, last_seen} (millis) or null
  access.statistic {uuid, key}           i64
  access.set_statistic {uuid, key, value}   bool
  access.last_death {uuid}               {dimension, x, y, z} or null
  datapacks.list                         list of {id, enabled, required, compatibility, source}   (datapacks)
  datapacks.refresh                      null                                                       (datapacks)
  datapacks.resource {name}              bytes or null                                              (datapacks)
  datapacks.resources {prefix}           list of text                                               (datapacks)
  datapacks.resource_pack {name}         text or null                                               (datapacks)
  datapacks.functions | function_tags    list of text                                               (datapacks)
  datapacks.scheduled                    list of {name, trigger_time}                               (datapacks)
  datapacks.schedule {function, delay, replace}    bool                                             (datapacks)
  datapacks.unschedule {name}            i64                                                        (datapacks)
  stopwatches.list                       list of text
  stopwatches.create | restart | remove {id}    bool
  stopwatches.elapsed {id}               f64 seconds or null
  ops                                    list of every operation name above
Errors besides INVALID: DENIED for a datapacks.* operation without the capability.

name: profile_lookup
signature: int32_t basalt_profile_lookup(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t token)

name: store_get
signature: int32_t basalt_store_get(const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
store_get: the value of `key` as a value document into `out` (length the full answer needs), ABSENT when the key is
not set, DENIED without capability `storage`.

name: store_set
signature: int32_t basalt_store_set(const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc: store_set: stores the value, or deletes the key when the value is null. OK, DENIED, INVALID.

name: data_read
signature: int32_t basalt_data_read(const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
data_read: the JSON document data/<name>.json of the plugin folder (a name with a '/' or ending in ".json" is a path
in the data folder; ".." and absolute paths are INVALID) decoded as a value: objects are maps, arrays lists, numbers
i64 when whole and f64 otherwise. Length the full answer needs, ABSENT when the file does not exist, INVALID when it
is not valid JSON, DENIED without capability `storage`.

name: data_write
signature: int32_t basalt_data_write(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
data_write: writes the value (bytes are INVALID, map keys are the object keys) as JSON to the same file,
through a temporary file and a rename, creating folders. OK, INVALID, DENIED.

name: config_value
signature: int32_t basalt_config_value(const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
config_value: the configuration (resources/config.toml, and every other .toml of the plugin folder as a table named
after its file) at a dotted key as a value: tables are maps, arrays lists, scalars as in config_*. The empty key is
the whole configuration. A key with '-' or '_' also finds the other spelling. Length the full answer needs, ABSENT
when there is no such key.

name: files_read
signature: int32_t basalt_files_read(const char *path, int32_t plen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: files_read: writes the file's bytes and returns the length the full answer needs; ABSENT when there is no file.

name: files_write
signature: int32_t basalt_files_write(const char *path, int32_t plen, const char *data, int32_t dlen)
doc:
files_write: replaces the file through a temporary sibling and a rename, creating folders. OK, DENIED, INVALID, or
ABSENT when the write failed.

name: files_exists
signature: int32_t basalt_files_exists(const char *path, int32_t plen)
doc: files_exists: 1 when the path exists in the folder or the packaged resources, else 0.

name: files_list
signature: int32_t basalt_files_list(const char *prefix, int32_t plen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
files_list: a value list of the names of the packaged and live files whose path starts with the prefix (the empty
path lists everything), sorted. Length the full answer needs.

name: files_stat
signature: int32_t basalt_files_stat(const char *path, int32_t plen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
files_stat: {kind: "file", "directory" or "other", size: i64, modified: i64 millis} of a path in the plugin folder,
ABSENT when it does not exist. Length the full answer needs.

name: files_walk
signature: int32_t basalt_files_walk(const char *path, int32_t plen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
files_walk: every path under a folder, parents first, directories ending in a slash, as a value list. ABSENT when
the folder does not exist.

name: files_delete
signature: int32_t basalt_files_delete(const char *path, int32_t plen, int32_t recursive)
doc:
files_delete: removes a file or an empty folder (recursive 0), or a folder and everything in it (recursive 1).
OK, ABSENT when there is nothing there, INVALID, DENIED.

name: files_capabilities
signature: int32_t basalt_files_capabilities(const char *path, int32_t plen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: files_capabilities: {atomic_move: bool, hard_links: bool} of the file system under a folder of the plugin folder.

name: service_register
signature: int32_t basalt_service_register(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t token)
doc:
service_register: offers `name` (it must be in this plugin's [exports] services, else DENIED; a taken name or an
empty one is INVALID). Returns a service handle. The handler runs with a completion-kind ctx whose value_result is
the call {name: text, caller: plugin id, args: value}; it answers inside the call with service_reply and cannot wait.
The service disappears when the plugin unloads or the handle is removed.

name: service_reply
signature: int32_t basalt_service_reply(int32_t ctx, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
service_reply: sets the value the caller receives (null is allowed). A second reply replaces the first. OK, STALE,
INVALID for a ctx that is not a service call or a bad value.

name: service_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_service_remove(int32_t service)
doc: service_remove: unregisters a service. OK, or ABSENT for an unknown handle.

name: service_has
signature: int32_t basalt_service_has(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: service_has: 1 when some loaded plugin offers the service, else 0.

name: service_list
signature: int32_t basalt_service_list(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: service_list: a value list of every service offered by loaded plugins, sorted.

name: service_call
signature: int32_t basalt_service_call(const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *args, int32_t alen, int32_t timeout, int32_t token)
doc:
service_call: calls `name` with the value `args` (alen 0 for null). Returns a request handle; basalt_callback(token,
ctx) later runs with a completion ctx whose value_result is {ok: true, value: value} or {ok: false, error: text}
(error is "unavailable" for a service nobody offers, "timeout", or "failed" when the handler trapped). `timeout` is
in ticks, 0 for 100. request_cancel drops the call if the handler has not run yet. INVALID for an empty name or a bad
value, ABSENT for a service nobody offers right now.

name: task_wait
signature: int32_t basalt_task_wait(int32_t ticks, int32_t token)
doc:
task_wait: the completion form of a wait: calls basalt_callback(token, ctx) after `ticks` ticks (at least 1)
with a completion ctx whose value_result is null. Returns a request handle; request_cancel drops it.

name: task_at
signature: int32_t basalt_task_at(const char *world, int32_t wlen, double x, double z, int32_t token)

name: world_by_name
signature: int32_t basalt_world_by_name(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc: world_by_name: the handle of the world with this name, 0 when there is none.

name: world_default
signature: int32_t basalt_world_default(void)
doc: world_default: the handle of the default world.

name: world_list
signature: int32_t basalt_world_list(int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc: world_list: writes the handles of every loaded world into `out` and returns the count the full list needs.

name: world_name
signature: int32_t basalt_world_name(int32_t world, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: world_name: the world's name as text, in the needed-length convention. STALE for an unloaded world.

name: world_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_get(int32_t world, const char *key, int32_t klen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_get: one property of the world by name, as a value. ABSENT for an unknown name, STALE for an unloaded world.
The names come from the host's own table, which `world_get(world, "properties")` lists as a list of maps
{name, type, writable}. They include: name, dimension (`minecraft:overworld`), seed, min_height, height, sea_level,
view_distance (writable), time (age in ticks), day_time (0 to 23999, writable), raining and thundering (bool),
difficulty (string, writable), difficulty_locked (bool, writable), spawn (list of x, y, z, writable), folder,
player_count, block_entity_count, tickable_block_entity_count, block_version, forced_chunks (flat list of x, z),
weather_times (map rain, thunder, clear in ticks, writable), clock (map total_ticks, rate, paused, markers),
spawn_rules (map limits, ticks_per by mob category, allow_monsters, allow_animals; writable), rules (list of game
rule names), plugin_data (bytes, the NBT plugins keep on the world, writable) and `tunable.<key>` (a number, writable;
the keys are void_damage, void_damage_amount, void_damage_offset and simulation_distance). Result: the length of the
encoded value the full answer needs.

name: world_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_set(int32_t world, const char *key, int32_t klen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
world_set: sets a writable property; the value is encoded as the property's type says. Two extra keys take effect
and are not readable: `weather` (map raining, thundering, bools) and `clock_rate` (float 0.00001 to 1000).
INVALID for a value of the wrong type or out of range, ABSENT for an unknown or read-only name. OK on success.

name: world_rule_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_rule_get(int32_t world, const char *name, int32_t nlen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_rule_get: a game rule as text ("true", "false" or a number). ABSENT for a rule the world does not know. The
names and types are listed by `worlds_data("game_rules")`.

name: world_rule_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_rule_set(int32_t world, const char *name, int32_t nlen, const char *value, int32_t vlen)
doc:
world_rule_set: sets a game rule from text. INVALID for a value that does not fit the rule's type, ABSENT for an
unknown rule.

name: world_create
signature: int32_t basalt_world_create(const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
world_create: creates a world from a map {name, dimension? (`minecraft:overworld`), type? (a world type name),
seed? (i64)} and returns its handle, or ABSENT when the server cannot create it. Needs `worldgen`. INVALID for a
missing name or a name that already exists. Making the world is slow server work and is not charged to the turn
budget, so call it alone in a turn.

name: world_unload
signature: int32_t basalt_world_unload(const char *name, int32_t nlen, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_unload: takes a world that holds no player out of play, saving it first with BASALT_WORLD_SAVE. ABSENT when it
is not loaded, INVALID for the default world or a world with players. Every handle of it turns STALE. Needs
`worldgen`.

name: world_delete
signature: int32_t basalt_world_delete(const char *name, int32_t nlen)
doc:
world_delete: deletes an unloaded, non-default world from the server's storage, by name only, never a path. ABSENT
for a name that is not a known unloaded world. Needs `worldgen`.

name: world_at
signature: int32_t basalt_world_at(int32_t world, double x, double z, int32_t token)
doc:
world_at: runs the plugin's callback `token` on the owner of the column (x, z) of this world, later, and returns a
request handle (the completion value is null; see core_values.h). With the default scheduler the owner is the plugin
thread and the callback runs on the next turn. Use it to touch positions the calling region does not own.

name: world_block_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_get(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t flags, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_block_get: the block state at the position as text with its properties. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded
and BASALT_WORLD_LOAD is not in `flags`. Needed-length convention.

name: world_block_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_set(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, const char *block, int32_t blen, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_block_set: puts the block (text with optional properties) at the position, telling watchers with
BASALT_WORLD_NOTIFY. INVALID for text that is not a block state, ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_state_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_state_get(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t flags)
doc: world_state_get: the state id at the position, or ABSENT as for `world_block_get`.

name: world_state_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_state_set(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t state, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_state_set: puts a state id at the position (BASALT_WORLD_NOTIFY in `flags`). INVALID for an id that is not a
state, ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_states_read
signature: int32_t basalt_world_states_read(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, int32_t count, int32_t *out, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_states_read: for `count` position triples at `positions`, writes one state id each (-1 where the chunk is not
loaded and BASALT_WORLD_LOAD is not set) into `out` and returns count. Bulk.

name: world_states_write
signature: int32_t basalt_world_states_write(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, const int32_t *states, int32_t count, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_states_write: writes `states[i]` at triple `i` of `positions` for `count` entries; returns how many were
written. BASALT_WORLD_NOTIFY tells watchers. Bulk.

name: world_fill
signature: int32_t basalt_world_fill(int32_t world, int32_t x1, int32_t y1, int32_t z1, int32_t x2, int32_t y2, int32_t z2, int32_t state, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_fill: fills the box between two corners (inclusive, in any order) with one state and returns how many blocks
changed. INVALID over 16777216 blocks. Chunks that are not loaded are skipped unless BASALT_WORLD_LOAD. Bulk.

name: world_section_read
signature: int32_t basalt_world_section_read(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t section_y, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t flags, int32_t *out)
doc:
world_section_read: the 4096 state ids of one section into `out` (room for 4096 i32). ABSENT when the chunk is not
loaded and BASALT_WORLD_LOAD is not set. Result 4096.

name: world_section_write
signature: int32_t basalt_world_section_write(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t section_y, int32_t chunk_z, const int32_t *states, int32_t flags)
doc: world_section_write: replaces one section from 4096 state ids. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_chunk_read
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_read(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t flags, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_chunk_read: every section of a chunk, lowest first, 4096 ids each; the result is the number of i32 the full
answer needs (sections * 4096), written only when it fits `cap`. ABSENT as for sections.

name: world_chunk_apply
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_apply(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, const int32_t *section_ys, int32_t count, const int32_t *states, int32_t flags, int32_t *previous)
doc:
world_chunk_apply: writes `count` whole sections of one chunk: `section_ys` lists the section indexes and `states`
holds 4096 ids per section (a negative id keeps the block). With BASALT_WORLD_RESEND the chunk is sent again. When
`previous` is not 0 it receives the 4096 ids that were there for each section. Returns the blocks changed, INVALID
for an index out of the world's height, ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded. Bulk.

name: world_changes_apply
signature: int32_t basalt_world_changes_apply(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, const int32_t *states, int32_t count, int32_t effects)
doc:
world_changes_apply: writes states at position triples, then runs `effects` (BASALT_WORLD_EFFECT_*) for the blocks
that changed. Returns how many changed. Bulk.

name: world_blocks_settle
signature: int32_t basalt_world_blocks_settle(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, const int32_t *previous, int32_t count, int32_t effects)
doc:
world_blocks_settle: runs `effects` for blocks already written at position triples; `previous` (or 0) holds the
state each had before. Returns how many positions were loaded.

name: world_blocks_notify
signature: int32_t basalt_world_blocks_notify(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, const int32_t *sources, int32_t count)
doc:
world_blocks_notify: tells the block at each position triple that a neighbour changed; `sources` (or 0) holds the
position triple of the neighbour that did. Returns how many positions were loaded.

name: world_blocks_reshape
signature: int32_t basalt_world_blocks_reshape(int32_t world, const int32_t *positions, int32_t count, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_blocks_reshape: lets the blocks around each position triple reshape to fit it; BASALT_WORLD_INDIRECT widens
it. Returns how many positions were reached.

name: world_state_valid
signature: int32_t basalt_world_state_valid(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t state)
doc:
world_state_valid: the state id `state` would settle to if it were put at the position (a fence joining, stairs
turning), written nowhere. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_tick_schedule
signature: int32_t basalt_world_tick_schedule(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t delay, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_tick_schedule: books a tick of the block (or its fluid with BASALT_WORLD_FLUID) `delay` ticks away. 1 when
booked, 0 when nothing there ticks.

name: world_tick_pending
signature: int32_t basalt_world_tick_pending(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z)
doc: world_tick_pending: 1 when a tick of the block at the position is already booked, else 0.

name: world_block_entity_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_entity_get(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_block_entity_get: the block entity at the position as a named NBT compound (id, x, y, z and its data) in
bytes, needed-length convention. ABSENT when the position holds none.

name: world_block_entity_edit
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_entity_edit(int32_t world, int32_t op, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen)
doc:
world_block_entity_edit: `op` 0 replaces the block entity data from the NBT compound, 1 creates one (empty NBT:
defaults), 2 removes it without touching the block (NBT ignored). ABSENT when the block owns no block entity or, for
2, there was none.

name: world_block_entities
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_entities(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_block_entities: the positions (flat triples) of the block entities of a loaded chunk; result is the number of
i32 the full list needs. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_data_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_data_get(int32_t world, int32_t scope, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_data_get: what plugins keep with the world as a named NBT compound in bytes. `scope` 0 is the world (x, y, z
ignored), 1 a loaded chunk (x, z are the chunk coordinates), 2 a block entity at x, y, z. ABSENT when there is none
or the chunk is not loaded. Needed-length convention.

name: world_data_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_data_set(int32_t world, int32_t scope, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen)
doc: world_data_set: replaces that data from an NBT compound. ABSENT as for `world_data_get` or when the NBT is rejected.

name: world_chunk_status
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_status(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z)
doc: world_chunk_status: 0 not loaded, 1 asked for and on its way, 2 loaded, 3 loaded and ticking.

name: world_chunk_load
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_load(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_chunk_load: loads the chunk now (BASALT_WORLD_GENERATE creates a missing one) and returns 1 when it is loaded
afterwards, else 0. May take a long time for a generated chunk; prefer `world_chunk_request`.

name: world_chunk_unload
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_unload(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z)
doc: world_chunk_unload: saves and drops a chunk nobody uses. 1 when dropped, 0 when a player still sees it.

name: world_chunk_request
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_request(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t flags, int32_t priority, int32_t token)
doc:
world_chunk_request: asks for a chunk without waiting (BASALT_WORLD_GENERATE creates it, a lower `priority` goes
first) and returns a request handle. Later basalt_callback(token, ctx) runs on the world's owner and `value_result`
answers `true` when the chunk is loaded, `false` when it never was. Cancel with `request_cancel`.

name: world_chunks_loaded
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunks_loaded(int32_t world, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc: world_chunks_loaded: the loaded chunks as flat (x, z) pairs; result is the number of i32 the full list needs.

name: world_chunk_hold
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_hold(int32_t world, const char *tag, int32_t tlen, const int32_t *chunks, int32_t count)
doc: world_chunk_hold: keeps `count` chunks (flat pairs) loaded for the holder `tag` until released. ABSENT when the world does not support held chunks.

name: world_chunk_release
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_release(int32_t world, const char *tag, int32_t tlen, const int32_t *chunks, int32_t count)
doc:
world_chunk_release: lets go of the chunks (flat pairs) the holder held; a negative `count` releases everything the
holder held. Returns OK.

name: world_chunk_held
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunk_held(int32_t world, const char *tag, int32_t tlen, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_chunk_held: the chunks (flat pairs) held for the holder `tag`. Result is the number of i32 the full list needs;
`world_call` "chunk_holders" answers the other way round, the holders of one chunk.

name: world_chunks_resend
signature: int32_t basalt_world_chunks_resend(int32_t world, const int32_t *chunks, int32_t count)
doc: world_chunks_resend: sends the chunks (flat pairs) again to every player of the world near them.

name: world_stored_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_stored_get(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_stored_get: the chunk exactly as stored on disk, a named NBT compound in bytes. ABSENT when the world has no
such chunk. Needed-length convention.

name: world_stored_put
signature: int32_t basalt_world_stored_put(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen)
doc:
world_stored_put: writes raw NBT as the stored chunk and flushes its region. ABSENT when the NBT is rejected or
the chunk cannot be replaced (it is loaded). Needs `worldgen`.

name: world_stored_list
signature: int32_t basalt_world_stored_list(int32_t world, int32_t region_x, int32_t region_z, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_stored_list: the chunks (flat pairs) stored in one region file. Result is the number of i32 the full list
needs.

name: world_light_at
signature: int32_t basalt_world_light_at(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t layer)
doc:
world_light_at: the light 0 to 15 at the position, `layer` 0 block light and 1 sky light, brought up to date. ABSENT
when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_light_read
signature: int32_t basalt_world_light_read(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t section_y, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t layer, int32_t flags, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_light_read: a section's light as 2048 bytes. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded (and BASALT_WORLD_LOAD is not
set) or has no light yet. Needed-length convention.

name: world_light_write
signature: int32_t basalt_world_light_write(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t section_y, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t layer, const char *nibbles, int32_t nlen)
doc:
world_light_write: replaces a section's light from 2048 bytes; it stands until blocks around change. INVALID for
another length.

name: world_light_check
signature: int32_t basalt_world_light_check(int32_t world, const int32_t *chunks, int32_t count, int32_t token)
doc:
world_light_check: works the light of chunks (flat pairs) out again off the tick thread and sends them. With a
non-zero `token` it returns a request handle and later calls basalt_callback(token, ctx), where `value_result` is the
number of chunks that were loaded; with token 0 it returns OK and does not wait.

name: world_biome_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_biome_get(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: world_biome_get: the biome id at the position (`minecraft:plains`). ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_biome_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_biome_set(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, const char *biome, int32_t blen)
doc: world_biome_set: sets the biome of the 4x4x4 cell at the position. ABSENT for an unknown biome or unloaded chunk.

name: world_biomes_read
signature: int32_t basalt_world_biomes_read(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, int32_t *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_biomes_read: a chunk's biomes as one i32 per cell, an index into `worlds_data("biomes")`. Result is the number
of i32 the full answer needs. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_biomes_write
signature: int32_t basalt_world_biomes_write(int32_t world, int32_t chunk_x, int32_t chunk_z, const int32_t *ids, int32_t count)
doc:
world_biomes_write: writes biome indexes in the same order (a negative index keeps the cell) and shows the chunk
again to its watchers. ABSENT when the chunk is not loaded.

name: world_sound
signature: int32_t basalt_world_sound(int32_t world, const char *sound, int32_t slen, const char *category, int32_t clen, double x, double y, double z, float volume, float pitch, int64_t seed)
doc:
world_sound: plays a sound id at a point to the players in range (16 blocks scaled by `volume`). `category` is one of
master, music, record, weather, block, hostile, neutral, player, ambient, voice, ui; empty means master. INVALID for
an unknown category.

name: world_particle
signature: int32_t basalt_world_particle(int32_t world, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
world_particle: shows a particle from a map {type (`minecraft:flame`), x, y, z, count? (1), offset_x, offset_y,
offset_z, speed (a number for all three axes) or speed_x, speed_y, speed_z, randomization? (0, 1, 2), force? (bool),
data? (list of numbers the particle's options read in order: a state id, a colour, a scale), item? (item id),
player? (name of the one player who sees it)}. INVALID for a missing type, ABSENT when the world has no effects.

name: world_level_event
signature: int32_t basalt_world_level_event(int32_t world, int32_t type, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t data, int32_t flags)
doc:
world_level_event: a level event (a sound or burst of particles the client knows by number) at a block; with
BASALT_WORLD_GLOBAL it reaches every player.

name: world_block_event
signature: int32_t basalt_world_block_event(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t first, int32_t second)
doc: world_block_event: a block event (a chest lid, a bell, a note) sent to the players watching the block.

name: world_explode
signature: int32_t basalt_world_explode(int32_t world, double x, double y, double z, float power, int32_t flags, int32_t source)
doc:
world_explode: an explosion of `power` at a point, from the entity id `source` (-1 none); BASALT_WORLD_BREAK and
BASALT_WORLD_FIRE gate block damage and fires. 1 when it happened.

name: world_lightning
signature: int32_t basalt_world_lightning(int32_t world, double x, double y, double z)
doc:
world_lightning: a lightning bolt at a point; returns the new bolt's entity id, or ABSENT when the spawn was
cancelled.

name: world_game_event
signature: int32_t basalt_world_game_event(int32_t world, const char *event, int32_t elen, double x, double y, double z, const char *source, int32_t slen)
doc:
world_game_event: raises a game event (`minecraft:block_place`) that sculk sensors in range hear; `source` is an
entity uuid or empty. INVALID for an empty name.

name: world_player_effect
signature: int32_t basalt_world_player_effect(int32_t player, const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_player_effect: a view-only effect for one player (a sound, particle, level event, a block shown as another,
a sign text, the player's own time, weather or border). `player` is a core player handle. `op` is one of
sound_at, sound_entity, stop_sound, particle_at, world_event, set_player_time, reset_player_time,
set_player_weather, block_change, block_damage, sign_text, open_sign, game_event, border_set, border_reset,
block_entity, post_effects, set_post_effects, entity_event, and the read-only properties player_time,
player_time_relative, player_weather, view_distance, simulation_distance (empty `args` reads, one value writes). `args` is a list of values, the positional arguments of that op (for
example sound_at: sound, category, x, y, z, volume, pitch, seed). The answer is a value (null when the op answers
nothing). ABSENT for an op that is not in the list, INVALID for arguments of the wrong type, STALE for a player who
left.

name: world_border_get
signature: int32_t basalt_world_border_get(int32_t world, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_border_get: the border as a map {center_x, center_z, size, target_size, lerp_ticks, damage_amount,
damage_buffer, warning_distance, warning_time}.

name: world_border_set
signature: int32_t basalt_world_border_set(int32_t world, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
world_border_set: applies the keys of that map that are present, plus `seconds` (f64): the size moves over that long
when positive. INVALID for a value out of range.

name: world_call
signature: int32_t basalt_world_call(int32_t world, const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
world_call: one operation of the world by name with a value argument and a value result, for what is too rare for an
import of its own. `args` is a map. `world_call(world, "ops", {})` returns the list of operation names the host
knows, generated from its table. Operations: save; use_item (x, y, z, face (0 to 5), item, yaw, pitch); survives
(x, y, z, state); bone_meal; break_block (x, y, z, tool?, enchantments?, drops?); drops (x, y, z, tool?, enchantments?,
by_entity?); signal (x, y, z, face, direct?); own_signal; analog_signal; fluid (x, y, z); fluid_flow; highest (x, z,
kind: surface, ocean_floor or motion_blocking); random_tick; grow_tree (x, y, z, sapling); place_tree; place_feature
and feature_ids; pois (types?, x, y, z, radius, occupancy); climate (x, y, z, in quarts); humidity and temperature;
beacon_scan; lightning_target (x, z); raids, raid_control, raid_bar, set_raid; sculk, hive, vault, creaking_heart;
dragon_fight, dragon_fight_action, dragon_fight_bar, place_end_gateway; random_sequence (id, kind, argument);
inhabited_time (chunk_x, chunk_z, value?); force_chunk (chunk_x, chunk_z, forced?); move_to_time_marker (marker);
chunk_holders (chunk_x, chunk_z, all?); break_speed (player name, x, y, z); structures (chunk_x, chunk_z; the structure
starts of a loaded chunk); locate_structure (structure, x, z, cells?, skip_existing?); locate_biome (biomes, x, y, z,
radius?, step?). Result: the length of the encoded value the
full answer needs. ABSENT for an unknown operation, INVALID for a bad argument, DENIED for an operation that needs a
capability.

name: structure_list
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_list(char *out, int32_t cap)
doc: structure_list: a value list with the id of every structure template (game data, saved and in memory).

name: structure_get
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_get(const char *id, int32_t ilen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
structure_get: the template as an unnamed NBT compound in the structure file format, in bytes. ABSENT for an id that
is not known.

name: structure_put
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_put(const char *id, int32_t ilen, const char *nbt, int32_t nlen, int32_t flags)
doc:
structure_put: keeps the template under the id (and in the world's generated folder with BASALT_WORLD_DISK).
INVALID for malformed NBT.

name: structure_remove
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_remove(const char *id, int32_t ilen, int32_t flags)
doc:
structure_remove: forgets the template (and deletes its generated file with BASALT_WORLD_DISK). ABSENT when it was
not there.

name: structure_file
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_file(const char *id, int32_t ilen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
structure_file: the path of the generated file that holds the template, as text (the id when it is only in memory).
ABSENT when the id is not known.

name: structure_capture
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_capture(int32_t world, int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z, int32_t size_x, int32_t size_y, int32_t size_z, int32_t flags, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
structure_capture: the blocks (and with BASALT_WORLD_ENTITIES the entities) of a box as a template, written to
`out` as an unnamed NBT compound. `world` names the world through its handle. ABSENT when the box is not loaded.

name: structure_scan
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_scan(const char *nbt, int32_t nlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
structure_scan: the blocks and jigsaws of a template as a placement would put them, with the world left alone.
`spec` is a map {x, y, z, rotation (0 to 3), mirror (0 to 2), pivot_x, pivot_z, block? (only this block id),
absolute? (bool)}. The result is a map {size: [x, y, z], blocks: [{x, y, z, state, nbt (bytes)}], jigsaws: [{x, y,
z, front, top, rollable, name, pool, target, final_state, placement_priority, selection_priority}]}.

name: structure_place
signature: int32_t basalt_structure_place(const char *nbt, int32_t nlen, const char *spec, int32_t slen)
doc:
structure_place: places a template given as NBT; `spec` is a map {world (name), x, y, z, rotation, mirror,
integrity? (f64), seed? (i64), entities? (bool), palette? (-1 picks at random)}. The loaded chunks it covers change.
ABSENT when the placement failed, INVALID for malformed NBT or a bad spec.

name: datafix_call
signature: int32_t basalt_datafix_call(const char *op, int32_t olen, const char *args, int32_t alen, char *out, int32_t cap)
doc:
datafix_call: the native data fixer. `op` is one of supports (type; answers a bool), types (answers a list of
type names), steps (type; answers [{version, sub_version, name}]), missing (type, from, to; answers the first step
that cannot run, or an empty string), legacy_state (id; the 1.13 {name, properties} of a `block << 4 | data` id),
modern_state (id; the current {name, properties}), upgrade (type, nbt (bytes), from, to; answers the fixed NBT as
